# Memory

**Append-only.** Never edit or delete existing entries below this point. If a past entry turns out
to be wrong, add a new entry that supersedes it — do not rewrite history. Never mark a task complete
in `docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` without a corresponding entry here.

Every agent reads this file (after `docs/DOMAIN_RULES.md`, before `docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`)
before starting any task, and appends an entry before reporting back.

## Standing Decisions

Short list of choices that override defaults. Agents read this section first, every time.

- **Custom Gantt only.** No commercial Gantt library (DHTMLX, Bryntum, Syncfusion). Hand-built
  virtualized SVG/Canvas, per `docs/PROJECT_AND_STACK.md`.
- **three.js is not used in v1.** Permitted only behind an explicit future feature flag, for a 3D
  cooler-model viewer on Project Registration only. It must never appear on Dashboard, Capacity,
  Matrix, Gantt or Planning.
- **CP-SAT never runs inside the FastAPI process.** Solver dispatch goes through Celery workers only.
- **The scheduler's behaviour is defined by `docs/DOMAIN_RULES.md`, never by the prototype.** The
  prototype (`reference/rpd-platform-prototype.html`) is a differential test oracle during P2 only,
  retired at P2 close. See P2-T01 through P2-T05 in `docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`.
- **No secrets in the repo. No `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. No raw SQL string interpolation.**
- **Financial fields (TCOGS, gross margin, selling price, customer name) are commercially sensitive
  — encrypted at rest, never logged.**
- **Docker Compose, not Kubernetes.**

   Commercialized/On Hold). Added because `docs/PROJECT_AND_STACK.md` §2 Project Registration

4. **Encrypted field set kept to exactly the four CLAUDE.md-named fields** (`tcogs_eur`,
   `selling_price_eur`, `gross_margin_pct`, `customer_name`). Adjacent financial-scoring inputs seen
   in the prototype (`capex`, `rm_savings_keur`, and the derived `roi`/`payback_yrs` export columns)
   are left plain/unencrypted and, for `roi`/`payback_yrs`, unpersisted entirely (computed values,
   not stored, to avoid a second driftable source of truth). Flagged for `security-auditor`'s
   P1-T06 review in case the encrypted set should be broadened beyond the literal CLAUDE.md list.
5. **"Live" vs "versioned snapshot" duplication is intentional**: `ProjectWorkflowStep` (mutable,
   current) coexists with `ScheduleRunProjectStep`/`ScheduleRunProjectOutcome` (immutable,
   per-run/versioned) because the product genuinely needs both — the Gantt's "solid vs hatched"
   planned/actual distinction needs a durable live record independent of any one solver run, while
   Versions & History (P5) needs immutable historical snapshots per run. Same pattern applied to
   priorities: `PriorityScore` (current, editable inputs) vs `PriorityApplicationRun` +
   `PriorityApplicationResult` (versioned "Apply Priorities" history), since
   `docs/PROJECT_AND_STACK.md` §2 says priority applications are versioned too, mirroring
   `ScheduleRun`.
6. **No FK pointer from `Project` to an "active schedule"**: instead `ScheduleRun.is_active` (and
   `PriorityApplicationRun.is_active`) is a single portfolio-wide flag, intended to be constrained to
   at-most-one-true via a **partial unique index that P1-T02's migration still needs to add**
   (`CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ... WHERE is_active`) — not expressible as a plain SQLAlchemy column
   constraint. Dashboard/Gantt/Capacity/Matrix all read the active run's snapshot rows, which is the
   mechanism satisfying Invariant I9 ("within_year count ... no independent calculation anywhere").
7. **UUID primary keys use Python-side `uuid.uuid4()` defaults**, not Postgres `gen_random_uuid()`,
   to avoid a `pgcrypto`/`uuid-ossp` extension dependency in the migration.
8. **`AuditLogEntry` immutability is only a code-level convention at this layer** (no `updated_at`,
   a docstring warning). True DB-enforced append-only (trigger rejecting UPDATE/DELETE, or REVOKE)
   is called out as a P1-T02 migration TODO — this model alone cannot enforce it.
9. **Currency rates**: `CurrencyRate` model included now (table only) even though seeding/the Admin
   endpoint is P1-T04, because `docs/DOMAIN_RULES.md` explicitly demands a config table exist ("Rates
   must be configurable at runtime ... store them in a config table, not in code") and it's
   referenced entity coverage for this task's acceptance criteria. `domain_constants.CURRENCY_RATE_SEED`
   holds only the documented v1 seed values for P1-T03/T04 to load, not a runtime source of truth.

### [2026-08-29 22:45] P1-T02 — backend-builder

**Did:** Wrote and verified the Alembic migration for the initial schema (all 18 tables from
P1-T01), against a real Postgres 17 instance (Docker was not running at session start but came up
cleanly after `open -a Docker`; not skipped). Set up `backend/alembic/` (async template,
`alembic init -t async`), pointed `alembic/env.py`'s `target_metadata` at `from models import Base;
Base.metadata`, and configured the DB URL via `RPD_DATABASE_URL` env var (async
`postgresql+asyncpg://` DSN) rather than a hardcoded/committed value in `alembic.ini`. Generated the
base migration via `alembic revision --autogenerate` against a live empty Postgres 17 container,
then hand-added: (1) the two partial unique indexes (`ux_schedule_runs_one_active` on
`schedule_runs (is_active) WHERE is_active`, `ux_priority_application_runs_one_active` on
`priority_application_runs (is_active) WHERE is_active`) enforcing Invariant I9's "at most one active
run" mechanism; (2) a `BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE` trigger (`trg_audit_log_entries_append_only`, backed
by a PL/pgSQL function `audit_log_entries_reject_mutation()`) on `audit_log_entries` that
unconditionally raises an exception on any UPDATE/DELETE attempt, enforcing the immutable
append-only audit log at the DB layer regardless of which role connects. Both additions have
explicit, hand-written `downgrade()` logic (index drops, trigger/function drops) since autogenerate
produces neither direction for DDL-only constructs.

**Verification performed (all against a live `postgres:17` Docker container, not just DDL-compile):**
- `alembic upgrade head` on a fresh DB: clean, all 19 tables present (18 app tables +
  `alembic_version`).
- Functional test of both partial unique indexes: first `is_active=true` row per table succeeds, a
  second `is_active=true` row on the same table raises `duplicate key value violates unique
  constraint`, additional `is_active=false` rows insert freely (multiple inactive rows coexist, only
  one active row is blocked) — confirmed for both `schedule_runs` and `priority_application_runs`.
- Functional test of the audit trigger: INSERT succeeds; UPDATE and DELETE against the same row both
  raise `audit_log_entries is append-only: <OP> is not permitted`, and the row is confirmed
  unmodified afterward. Tested as the same role that owns the table (`rpd`), not a restricted role —
  confirms the trigger (not a REVOKE-based approach, which would need per-role grants) blocks even a
  privileged/owning connection, which was the explicit rationale for choosing a trigger.
- `alembic downgrade base`: clean.
- Full round-trip repeated twice (`upgrade head` → `downgrade base` → `upgrade head` →
  `downgrade base`) to catch anything that only breaks on a second pass — this is what caught the
  enum-type leak below. Final state after downgrade: zero tables besides `alembic_version` (empty,
  standard Alembic behavior — the bookkeeping table itself is not expected to be dropped), zero
  custom enum types, zero functions, zero non-`alembic_version` indexes.

**Two P1-T01 model bugs found and fixed during this verification (both are `models/` changes, not
just migration changes — flagging clearly since P1-T01 was already reviewed and accepted; this is a
"past entry turns out to be wrong" case per the memory protocol, not a silent rewrite):**

1. **Enum values were being persisted as Python member *names*, not *values*.** SQLAlchemy's `Enum`
   type defaults to using `[e.name for e in enum_class]` to generate DB-side ENUM labels and to bind
   values, unless `values_callable` is explicitly passed — it does NOT use `.value` automatically
   even for `str`-mixin enums. This directly contradicted `models/enums.py`'s own module docstring
   ("Enums whose member *values* (not just names) must match docs/DOMAIN_RULES.md's vocabulary
   exactly"). Confirmed empirically: before the fix, `hub_name`'s Postgres ENUM labels were
   `RD_GREECE, RD_INDIA, PD_INDIA, PD_ROMANIA, OEM_HCK, OEM_SELTEK` instead of `R&D-Greece, R&D-India,
   PD-India, PD-Romania, OEM-HCK, OEM-Seltek`; same class of bug on every other `Enum(...)` column
   (`project_category` stored `A_PLUS` instead of `A+`, `project_status` stored `IN_BUYOFF` instead
   of `In Buyoff`, etc. — 17 occurrences across `chamber.py`, `currency.py`, `engineer.py`,
   `hub.py`(×2), `priority.py`(×5), `project.py`(×4), `schedule.py`(×2), `workflow.py`). **Fixed** by
   adding `values_callable=lambda enum_cls: [e.value for e in enum_cls]` to all 17 call sites (a
   scripted regex replacement, then spot-checked). Regenerated the autogenerate migration afterward
   and confirmed via `pg_enum` that every enum type now carries the exact DOMAIN_RULES.md-vocabulary
   string values. This would otherwise have broken every raw-SQL/reporting/export path reading
   directly from Postgres, and any future seed-data or scheduling-dataclass comparison against the
   DB that expected the documented values.
2. **`op.drop_table()` does not emit `DROP TYPE` for inline `sa.Enum(...)` columns** — a known
   Alembic/Postgres quirk (each `sa.Enum(...)` instance in an autogenerated script is scoped to its
   own `create_table`/`drop_table` call, not tracked across the migration file the way
   `MetaData.drop_all()` tracks it). Confirmed empirically: after the first `downgrade base`, all 12
   custom enum types (`lab_region`, `hub_name`, `project_category`, etc.) remained in the database,
   and a subsequent `alembic upgrade head` failed with `DuplicateObjectError: type "lab_region"
   already exists`. **Fixed** by adding explicit `DROP TYPE IF EXISTS <name>` statements for all 12
   enum types at the end of `downgrade()`, after all `drop_table` calls (types can't be dropped while
   still referenced by a column). Re-verified the full upgrade→downgrade→upgrade→downgrade cycle
   afterward with zero leftover types.
3. **Autogenerate also emitted one call site missing the `sa.` prefix**: `sa.ARRAY(Enum(...))` for
   `Engineer.allowed_categories` (should be `sa.ARRAY(sa.Enum(...))`) — a cosmetic Alembic rendering
   quirk specific to `ARRAY`-wrapped `Enum` columns, not a functional bug like #1/#2, but would have
   caused a `NameError: name 'Enum' is not defined` at migration runtime since only `sa`, `op`, and
   `postgresql` are imported in the generated script. Fixed by hand.

**Files touched:**
- `backend/alembic.ini` — new (from `alembic init -t async`), `sqlalchemy.url` left as the
  unmodified placeholder (`driver://user:pass@localhost/dbname`, not a secret/real DSN) since
  `env.py` overrides it from `RPD_DATABASE_URL` at runtime.
- `backend/alembic/env.py` — `target_metadata = Base.metadata` (imported from `models`), sys.path
  fallback so `from models import Base` resolves regardless of invocation CWD, `RPD_DATABASE_URL`
  env var wiring, async engine (unmodified from the `-t async` template otherwise — `asyncpg` via
  `async_engine_from_config` + `run_sync`).
- `backend/alembic/script.py.mako`, `backend/alembic/README` — untouched, default template output.
- `backend/alembic/versions/419f196fd00b_initial_schema.py` — the initial schema migration: all 18
  `CREATE TABLE` statements (autogenerated, hand-verified against every model file), plus the two
  hand-written partial unique indexes, the hand-written audit-log append-only trigger + function, and
  the hand-written enum-type downgrade cleanup, each with matching `downgrade()` logic.

  `schedule.py`, `workflow.py` — added `values_callable=lambda enum_cls: [e.value for e in
  enum_cls]` to all 17 `Enum(...)` column-type constructor calls (bug #1 above). No other changes to
  these files; column names, nullability, FKs, constraints all unchanged from P1-T01.

  `cryptography` for migration generation/verification; already covered by `backend/.gitignore`
  (`.venv/`), not committed.

**Decisions:**
1. **Both hand-written mechanisms (partial indexes, audit trigger) live in the single initial-schema
   migration file**, not a separate follow-up migration — they're conceptually part of "the initial
   schema" (a fresh DB should never pass through a state where the active-run invariant or audit
   immutability isn't enforced), and the task's phrasing ("the Alembic migration for the initial
   schema") reads as one coherent unit of work rather than mandating a second file.
2. **Trigger over REVOKE for audit-log append-only enforcement** (task allowed either): a trigger is
   enforced for any role that can reach the table, including the table owner/migration role itself,
   whereas REVOKE only protects against roles it's explicitly applied to and would need to be kept in
   sync with every future role (API runtime role, admin scripts, etc.) — explained in an in-file
   comment. Verified this by running the UPDATE/DELETE negative tests as the table-owning role (`rpd`)
   and confirming they still fail.
3. **`op.execute()` with static, non-interpolated SQL strings for the trigger/function/index DDL** is
   not a violation of CLAUDE.md's "no raw SQL string interpolation" non-negotiable — that rule targets
   the application data-access layer handling untrusted/variable input (P3's query construction), not
   static schema DDL in a migration file where the only "interpolation" is Python f-strings substituting
   fixed, hardcoded identifier constants (`_SCHEDULE_RUNS_ACTIVE_IDX` etc.) defined in the same file,
   never request/user data. Flagging this reasoning explicitly for security-auditor's P1-T06 review in
   case a stricter reading is intended.
4. **`RPD_DATABASE_URL` chosen as the env var name** (not e.g. `DATABASE_URL`) to keep it
   unambiguous and namespaced alongside `RPD_FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (`models/types.py`, P1-T01) — no
   other `RPD_*` env var convention was established yet, so this sets it for `core`/settings config
   in P3.
5. **Did not add btree indexes on FK columns** (e.g. `projects.hub_id`, `audit_log_entries.hub_id`)
   beyond what SQLAlchemy/Alembic autogenerate produced from the P1-T01 models (which only indexes
   PKs, unique constraints, and explicit `index=True` columns — none were marked `index=True` in
   P1-T01). Hub-scoped row filtering (P3-T03) will filter on `hub_id` for nearly every query, so an
   index there is very likely warranted for production query performance — flagged here rather than
   speculatively added, since it's a P1-T01 model-level decision (`index=True` on the mapped column)
   this task didn't have a mandate to make unilaterally, and no seed-scale data exists yet to profile
   against. Worth a follow-up task or P1-T01 addendum before P1 closes.
6. Migration file left named `419f196fd00b_initial_schema.py` (the second-generated revision ID,
   after the first attempt was discarded for the enum-name bug) rather than renamed to something more
   readable — matches the project's now-only migration file 1:1 with no ambiguity, and hand-renaming
   Alembic revision-ID-prefixed filenames independently of the `revision:` string inside is a common
   source of drift bugs, so left alone.

**Deviations from plan:** None from the P1-T02 acceptance criteria itself (upgrade/downgrade both
verified clean against real Postgres 17). The two model-file bug fixes (enum `values_callable`, one
missing `sa.` prefix caught only in the discarded first-generation file) go beyond "write the
migration" into "fix P1-T01 model bugs the migration surfaced" — recorded per the memory protocol's
"if a past entry turns out to be wrong, add a new entry that supersedes it" instruction rather than
silently patched with no trace. P1-T01's MEMORY.md entry and the orchestrator's review entry are left
untouched (append-only); this entry is the correction.

**Broke / discovered:** The two bugs above (enum `values_callable` missing; `DROP TYPE` not emitted
by `op.drop_table()` for inline enums) — both now fixed and re-verified. No other issues found. Confirmed
Docker was available in this environment (unlike P1-T01's session) after `open -a Docker`; a
`postgres:17` container was used for every verification step in this entry, not skipped or
DDL-compile-only.

**Gate result:** N/A — no gate check run yet (P1's gate is qa-inspector + security-auditor PASS, not
yet invoked; this task's own status is REVIEW pending orchestrator sign-off, same pattern as P1-T01).

**Next:** Orchestrator review of this task (in particular the two model-bug fixes to files outside
this task's literal file list, and the trigger-vs-REVOKE / raw-SQL-in-migration reasoning in
Decisions #2/#3) before marking P1-T02 DONE. Then P1-T03 (seed data import, depends on P1-T02) can
proceed — note for whoever picks it up: seed data must use the corrected enum *values* (e.g.
`"R&D-Greece"`, `"A+"`, `"In Buyoff"`), not the old (buggy) member names, when constructing
INSERTs or ORM objects. P1-T04 (currency rate endpoint) can also proceed in parallel, same
dependency. Flagging Decision #5 (no FK-column indexes yet) for whoever does P1-T01-scope cleanup or
P3-T03 (hub-scoped filtering) to revisit before that endpoint work assumes fast `hub_id` filtering.

   project's actual scheduling start as

   project, `actualStart` is merely a *lower-bound scheduling hint* the greedy algorithm clamps and
   then still searches forward from, not a real "this already happened on week N" fact. Only for
   `frozen` projects does `actualStart` mean what `Project.actual_start_week`'s docstring says it

### [2026-08-30 11:10] P1-T07 — backend-builder

**Did:** Remediated the security-auditor's P1-T06 High finding: `audit_log_entries`'s append-only
enforcement did not cover `TRUNCATE`. Reproduced the exact gap live first, then fixed it with a new
Alembic migration (chained after, not editing, the already-applied `419f196fd00b_initial_schema.py`),
then re-verified live that the fix closes the gap without regressing the existing UPDATE/DELETE
protection, then added a dedicated pytest module and ran the full backend suite.

**Reproduction (before the fix), against a disposable `postgres:17` Docker container, `alembic
upgrade head` on `419f196fd00b` only, connected as the `rpd` role — the same role
migrations/seed/API code all use, not a more-privileged one):**
- `INSERT` a row into `audit_log_entries` → succeeds, row count 1.
- `UPDATE audit_log_entries SET action = 'tampered'` → correctly rejected:
  `ERROR: audit_log_entries is append-only: UPDATE is not permitted (row id=...)`.
- `TRUNCATE audit_log_entries;` → **succeeded** (`TRUNCATE TABLE`), row count afterward: **0**. Gap
  confirmed exactly as security-auditor's P1-T06 finding described: the `BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE
  ... FOR EACH ROW` trigger never fires on `TRUNCATE`, a distinct statement-level operation with its
  own trigger event type in Postgres.

**Fix:** New migration `backend/alembic/versions/ba3881d85b55_audit_log_truncate_protection.py`,
`down_revision = '419f196fd00b'`. Adds a second trigger,
`trg_audit_log_entries_append_only_truncate`, `BEFORE TRUNCATE ON audit_log_entries FOR EACH
STATEMENT`, backed by a **new sibling function** `audit_log_entries_reject_truncate()` (chose sibling
over reusing/overloading `audit_log_entries_reject_mutation()` — see Decision #1 below for the
reasoning, which is also written directly into the migration's module docstring so it survives
independently of this MEMORY.md entry). `downgrade()` drops the trigger then the function, mirroring
419f196fd00b's own trigger/function downgrade pattern exactly.

**Post-fix live verification (same container, `alembic upgrade head` now includes both migrations,
same `rpd` role):**
- `INSERT` → succeeds, row count 1 (`INSERT 0 1`).
- `UPDATE audit_log_entries SET action = 'tampered'` → still rejected:
  `ERROR: audit_log_entries is append-only: UPDATE is not permitted (row id=...)` — **no regression**,
  tested explicitly, not assumed.
- `DELETE FROM audit_log_entries` → still rejected:
  `ERROR: audit_log_entries is append-only: DELETE is not permitted (row id=...)` — **no regression**.
- `TRUNCATE audit_log_entries;` → **now rejected**:
  `ERROR: audit_log_entries is append-only: TRUNCATE is not permitted` (raised by the new
  `audit_log_entries_reject_truncate()` function, confirmed via the `CONTEXT:` line naming it).
- Final row count after all four attempts: **1**, unchanged — the row inserted for this test is still
  exactly as it was.

**Migration up/down/up-again rigor (same container, via raw `alembic` CLI, not just pytest):**
- `alembic downgrade -1` (drop only the new migration) → `pg_trigger` shows only
  `trg_audit_log_entries_append_only` remains (the original UPDATE/DELETE one); confirmed `TRUNCATE`
  succeeds again at this intermediate state (proves the new trigger, and only the new trigger, was
  removed — the original migration's own trigger is untouched by this migration's downgrade).
- `alembic upgrade head` → both triggers present again
  (`trg_audit_log_entries_append_only`, `trg_audit_log_entries_append_only_truncate`).
- `alembic downgrade base` → clean, only `alembic_version` table remains, zero custom enum types
  (confirms this migration's downgrade doesn't interfere with `419f196fd00b`'s own enum-type cleanup,
  which runs after all table drops in the base migration).
- `alembic upgrade head` again → clean, both triggers present.
- `alembic downgrade base` again → clean, zero enum types. Full up→down→up→down cycle, matching the
  rigor P1-T02 established as this project's standard.

**Files touched:**
- `backend/alembic/versions/ba3881d85b55_audit_log_truncate_protection.py` — new migration (see
  Fix above). Module docstring documents the reproduction, the reuse-vs-sibling reasoning, and the
  design-property continuity with `419f196fd00b`.
- `backend/tests/test_audit_truncate_trigger.py` — new, additive pytest module (4 tests: INSERT
  still works, TRUNCATE now rejected + row survives, UPDATE still rejected (no regression), DELETE
  still rejected (no regression)). Deliberately a **new file**, not an edit to
  `backend/tests/test_audit_trigger.py` (P1-T05/qa-inspector's file, which per
  `docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` was still `IN_PROGRESS` at the start of this session) — avoids
  colliding with concurrent qa-inspector work while still giving this fix its own repeatable,
  CI-runnable verification, not just the one-off manual Docker session recorded above. Uses the same
  `db_session` fixture / `testcontainers` pattern already established in `tests/conftest.py`. Ran
  standalone (`pytest tests/test_audit_truncate_trigger.py tests/test_audit_trigger.py -v` — 8/8
  pass, confirming no interaction/ordering issue between the two trigger test modules) and as part of
  the full suite (`pytest tests/ -q` — 62/62 pass, up from the 58 that existed before this task,
  confirming zero regressions anywhere else in the backend test suite). Did **not** edit
  `backend/tests/test_migrations.py` (also qa-inspector's file) even though its trigger-name
  assertions (`assert "trg_audit_log_entries_append_only" in _trigger_names(url)`) use `in` against a
  set rather than an exact-set equality check, so it already passes unmodified with the new trigger
  present — a stronger assertion adding the new trigger name there would be a reasonable follow-up
  but risks colliding with qa-inspector's own in-flight edits to that file; left for qa-inspector or
  a future pass to add if wanted.
- `docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` (P1-T07 → REVIEW), `docs/MEMORY.md` (this entry).

**Decisions:**
1. **Sibling function (`audit_log_entries_reject_truncate`) over reusing/extending
   `audit_log_entries_reject_mutation()`.** The existing function's exception message references
   `COALESCE(OLD.id, NULL)`; a `TRUNCATE` trigger is statement-level and has no `OLD`/`NEW` row bound
   at all (not merely NULL — genuinely unavailable in that context). It would be possible to make one
   shared function handle both by guarding the `OLD` reference behind an `IF TG_OP = 'TRUNCATE' THEN
   ... ELSE ... OLD.id ... END IF` (PL/pgSQL only evaluates the branch taken, so `OLD` would never be
   dereferenced in the `TRUNCATE` path), but that makes a single function silently serve two
   structurally different trigger kinds — harder to audit at a glance, and one bad future edit
   (someone moving the `OLD.id` reference outside the guard without noticing the function is shared
   between a row-level and a statement-level trigger) would break both trigger kinds at once, possibly
   inconsistently. A small, single-purpose sibling function that never references `OLD`/`NEW` at all
   removes that whole class of risk, at the cost of two short functions instead of one. Both functions
   preserve the same "enforced regardless of DB role" property `419f196fd00b`'s comment block
   originally argued for — verified this explicitly (see live verification above: tested as `rpd`,
   the table-owning role, not a restricted one, for both the UPDATE/DELETE and the TRUNCATE case).
2. **New migration, not an edit to `419f196fd00b_initial_schema.py`** — per this task's explicit
   instruction and standard Alembic convention (that migration is already applied/live; a schema
   change belongs in a new revision, chained via `down_revision`). Generated via
   `alembic revision -m "audit log truncate protection"` so the revision ID/chain is
   Alembic-authored, not hand-invented, then hand-filled with the trigger/function DDL (the same
   pattern `419f196fd00b` itself used for its own hand-written trigger — autogenerate cannot produce
   trigger DDL either direction).
3. **`op.execute()` with static, non-interpolated SQL strings** for the new trigger/function DDL —
   same reasoning `419f196fd00b`'s own Decision #3 already recorded (this targets fixed, hardcoded
   schema DDL constants defined in the same file, never request/user data; not a violation of the
   "no raw SQL string interpolation" rule, which targets the application data-access layer).
4. **Did not touch anything beyond the TRUNCATE gap** — no DB role separation, no REVOKE changes, no
   broader audit-log hardening. Per this task's explicit scope instruction and per P1-T06's own
   finding #3 (DB role hygiene, Low severity) being explicitly deferred to P6.

**Deviations from plan:** None from P1-T07's acceptance criteria. One minor scope addition beyond the
literal task text: added a new pytest test file (not required by the acceptance criteria, which only

check durable (re-run in CI going forward) rather than a one-time manual finding, without touching any
file qa-inspector might be concurrently editing.

**Broke / discovered:** None. Confirmed the exact P1-T06 finding reproduces byte-for-byte as
described (TRUNCATE succeeds, wipes the table, as the app's own role) before fixing it, and confirmed
the fix closes it without any regression to the existing UPDATE/DELETE protection or to any other

**Decisions:**
1. **Function-scoped `AsyncEngine` per test, not a shared session-scoped one.** First version of
   `db_session` shared one `AsyncEngine`/connection pool across the whole session; this broke with
   `sqlalchemy.exc.InterfaceError: cannot perform operation: another operation is in progress` as soon
   as more than one test ran, because asyncpg connections are bound to the event loop they were
   created in and pytest-asyncio's default "auto" mode gives each test function its own event loop.
   Switched to creating (and disposing) a fresh `AsyncEngine` per test, while still sharing the one
   Postgres *container* for the whole session (container startup, not engine/connection-pool creation,
   is the expensive part) — documented inline in `conftest.py` so a future reader doesn't reintroduce
   the bug by "optimizing" it back to session scope.
2. **`alembic/` excluded from the measured coverage percentage, but not from actual testing.** The
   migration file(s) run via `subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "alembic", ...])` in
   `test_migrations.py`/`test_seed_scripts.py`, matching how P1-T02 was verified by hand — this
   subprocess boundary means `coverage.py`'s in-process line tracking doesn't attribute those executed
   lines to this pytest run. Considered wiring up `coverage run --parallel-mode` inside the subprocess
   invocation to close this gap, but judged not worth the added complexity/fragility given the
   migration file is already exhaustively *functionally* verified (every `CREATE TABLE`, both partial
   indexes, both audit triggers, the enum-type cleanup, exercised on both `upgrade` and `downgrade`,
   twice) — a coverage percentage on a DDL script is a much weaker signal than "did the DDL actually
   produce the right schema and did the schema actually behave correctly," which this suite already
   proves. Documented this reasoning inline in `pyproject.toml`'s `addopts` comment so it isn't
   mistaken for an oversight. `backend/` overall, even fully excluding `alembic/`, clears 70% by a wide
   margin (97.93% on the measured scope) — this decision has zero effect on whether the acceptance
   criterion is met.
3. **`session.rollback()` expires all ORM attributes — captured IDs as plain Python variables before
   calling it**, in both `test_audit_trigger.py` and (following the same fix) confirmed present in
   backend-builder's `test_audit_truncate_trigger.py`. Discovered this the hard way: `entry.id`
   accessed after `db_session.rollback()` triggers SQLAlchemy's expired-attribute lazy-reload, which
   tries to issue a synchronous SELECT outside of an awaited context in `AsyncSession`, raising
   `sqlalchemy.exc.MissingGreenlet`. Fixed by capturing `entry_id = entry.id` immediately after
   creation, before any rollback in the same test.
4. **Committing (not just flushing) an audit-log entry before attempting the illegal
   UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE against it.** `session.rollback()` rolls back the *entire* session-level
   transaction back to the last `commit()` (a SAVEPOINT release, under
   `join_transaction_mode="create_savepoint"`), not just the failed statement — an INSERT that was
   only `flush()`ed (not `commit()`ted) in the same session transaction as a later failed UPDATE would
   be rolled back too, making "confirm the row is unchanged post-rollback" impossible to assert
   correctly. Fixed by committing the INSERT as its own savepoint first.
5. **Extended `test_migrations.py` to assert the P1-T07 TRUNCATE trigger's presence/absence**, rather
   than leaving it untested by my migration-cycle test just because it landed after I'd already
   written the file. `alembic upgrade head`/`downgrade base` walk the whole revision chain
   regardless of how many revisions exist, so no structural change was needed beyond adding two more
   `assert ... in/not in _trigger_names(url)` lines — verified this doesn't require bumping
   `EXPECTED_TABLE_COUNT` (the new migration adds a trigger + function, no new table).
6. **Left backend-builder's `tests/test_audit_truncate_trigger.py` in place rather than absorbing it
   into `tests/test_audit_trigger.py` or rewriting it.** It is correct, well-scoped (INSERT-still-works,
   TRUNCATE-rejected, UPDATE/DELETE-no-regression), doesn't duplicate anything in my own suite, and
   its own module docstring explains why it was written as a separate file specifically to avoid
   colliding with this in-flight task. Re-attributed it honestly in this entry rather than either
   silently claiming it as my own work or silently deleting another agent's legitimate, reviewed
   contribution.
7. **Did not add `factory_boy`/`pytest-timeout`/other new dev dependencies** beyond what
   `pyproject.toml`'s existing `dev` extra already lists (`pytest`, `pytest-asyncio`, `pytest-cov`,
   `testcontainers[postgres]`) — hand-rolled factories and plain `subprocess`/`asyncio.run()` timing
   were sufficient for this task's scope.

**Deviations from plan:** None from P1-T05's own acceptance criteria (≥70% coverage on `backend/`
excluding `backend/scheduling/`; migrations tested up and down — both satisfied with substantial
margin). One scope expansion beyond the original P1-T01–T04 file list: incorporated P1-T07's
mid-session migration (`ba3881d85b55`) into `test_migrations.py`'s assertions, since it's now part of
what "the initial migration" means as of this session — flagged explicitly rather than silently
ignored or silently claimed as pre-planned scope.

**Broke / discovered:** No bugs found in `models/`, the migrations, or the seed scripts — everything
behaved exactly as documented in the P1-T01 through P1-T04 (and P1-T07) MEMORY.md entries, confirmed
independently rather than taken on faith. Two test-infrastructure bugs found and fixed while building
this suite (both in test code, not application code — see Decisions #1 and #3/#4 above): the
session-scoped-engine/per-test-event-loop `InterfaceError`, and the `session.rollback()`-expires-
attributes `MissingGreenlet` error. Both are common SQLAlchemy-2.0-async-testing pitfalls, not
findings about P1's shipped code.

**Gate result:** Reporting PASS for this task's own scope (backend model/migration test suite,
qa-inspector's half of P1's gate) — **64/64 tests pass, 97.93% coverage on the measured scope

**Design — dataclass contract:**

`ScheduleInput`: `projects: tuple[ProjectInput,...]`, `engineers: tuple[EngineerInput,...]`,
`chambers: tuple[ChamberInput,...]`, `workflow_steps: tuple[WorkflowStepTemplate,...]` (defaults to
the canonical 14-step template derived from `domain_constants.WORKFLOW_STEP_TEMPLATE_SEED`, but
overridable — deliberately, so P2-T05's golden-file fixtures can exercise one rule with a 1-2 step
template instead of always paying for all 14, per the `scheduling-algorithms` skill's "small
fixtures, one rule per fixture" guidance), `current_week`/`horizon_weeks`/`within_year_week`
(default to `domain_constants`' 31/78/52, also overridable for the same fixture-focus reason — e.g.
a "left-out at horizon" fixture doesn't need a full 78-week horizon to prove the point).

`ScheduleOutput`: `project_outcomes: tuple[ProjectScheduleOutcome,...]` — **exactly one entry per
input project**, sorted by `project_id` (caller-order-independent, see determinism note below) — and
`scheduling_order: tuple[str,...]`, the exact sequence the greedy walk processed schedulable
projects in (excludes excluded-status projects entirely), useful for P2-T02's differential oracle
and for debugging without re-deriving the sort.

`ProjectScheduleOutcome` distinguishes, as explicit, mutually-exclusive-where-it-matters booleans:
`excluded` (status outside the four schedulable statuses — never fed into the greedy walk at all,
per the task's explicit instruction that this be distinguishable from `left_out`), `left_out` (fed
in, searched, no feasible window before horizon, or no leader, or no eligible chamber for some lab
step), `eng_conflict`/`overlap` (I1/I2, only possible when `frozen=True`), `cat_not_allowed`
(warning only, never blocks scheduling), `spillover`/`within_year` (mutually exclusive whenever
`!left_out and !excluded`), plus two diagnostic-only fields (`no_leader`, `no_chamber_step_id`) that
aren't literal DOMAIN_RULES.md outcome flags but cheaply distinguish *why* a project was
`left_out`/never-booked, which I expect P2-T04's invariant validator to find useful. `steps` holds
whatever `StepSchedule`s were successfully booked, even for a `left_out` project that failed partway
through (see the "partial LEFT_OUT" ambiguity resolution below) — deliberately raw/primitive
(`assigned_engineer_id`, `assigned_chamber_id`, `start_week`, `end_week`, `duration_weeks` per step)
rather than pre-aggregated, so P2-T04's validator can independently recompute I1/I2/I6/I7 from first
principles instead of trusting anything this module aggregates.

IDs (`project_id`/`engineer_id`/`chamber_id`/`step_id`) are plain `str`, not `uuid.UUID` or any
`backend/models/` type — a pure function has no reason to demand a specific ID representation, and
it keeps future golden-file fixtures (P2-T05) readable (`"proj-1"` instead of a UUID literal).

**Ambiguities resolved by reading the prototype's actual scheduler (`qm`), per this task's explicit
instruction — DOMAIN_RULES.md's text is authoritative for all of these; the prototype was consulted
only where DOMAIN_RULES.md is silent, and every resolution below is a judgement call I made, not a
literal restatement of prototype behaviour where that would have contradicted DOMAIN_RULES.md:**

1. **"Concurrent project count" vs. "0.5 consumption per project-week" for lab-step capacity gating
   (task explicitly flagged this as needing re-derivation, not the obvious reading).** Resolved
   primarily from DOMAIN_RULES.md itself, cross-referencing Invariant I2 ("No chamber exceeds `max`
   concurrent projects in any week") against Invariant I7 ("Total lab load per hub = Σ(lab step
   durations × 0.5)... must reconcile with the Capacity surface") — these are two different things:
   I2 is a per-week, per-chamber, **unweighted integer project-count** gate; I7 is a separate,
   hub-level **reporting** aggregate that happens to use a 0.5 weighting. Confirmed against the
   prototype's actual gate check (`(l[f.id][d]||0)>=f.max`, a raw increment-by-1-per-project compare
   against `f.max`, no 0.5 anywhere near the booking path) and its separate reporting function `xi`
   (`n+=l*.5`, only used for a lab-load *display* aggregate, never for booking). **Decision:** the
   booking gate is a plain integer project-count compare against `chamber.max_concurrent`; the 0.5
   multiplier is not modelled in `backend/scheduling/` at all (no I7-style aggregate is computed here
   — P2-T04's validator, or a later reporting layer, computes it independently from `StepSchedule`'s
   raw `duration_weeks` per step, which is exactly what "recompute independently, don't trust an
   aggregate this module produces" is for).
2. **Earliest-start floor for a non-frozen project's search (the single biggest, most consequential
   decision in this task — flagged loudly for P2-T02/T03/T04 to specifically scrutinize).**
   DOMAIN_RULES.md says only "Non-frozen projects advance `w` until a free window is found" — it
   never states what `w` starts at. The prototype fills this gap with
   `h = Math.max(actualStart, CURRENT_WEEK - 6)`, treating every project's `actualStart` (even
   non-frozen ones) as a soft lower-bound hint. **Decision: did NOT replicate this.** Two
   independent reasons, both substantive, not just "prototype vs. spec" pedantry: (a) the
   already-reviewed-and-accepted P1 data model (`docs/MEMORY.md` P1-T03 entry, Decision #2,
   orchestrator-endorsed) populates `Project.actual_start_week` **only for frozen projects**
   specifically because a non-frozen project's `actualStart` "is merely a lower-bound scheduling
   hint... not a real 'this already happened on week N' fact" — building this scheduler around a
   field the accepted upstream data model deliberately nulls for non-frozen projects would silently
   resurrect an ambiguity P1 already closed in the other direction; (b) the "-6" offset has zero
   textual basis anywhere in DOMAIN_RULES.md and is exactly the kind of unexplained magic constant
   this task's own brief warns against silently transliterating. Implemented instead: a non-frozen
   project's search starts at `current_week` (you cannot schedule new, non-frozen work in the past),
   and if `ProjectInput.actual_start_week` happens to be populated (the field remains legal to set on
   a non-frozen project in this pure dataclass, even though current seed data never does) and exceeds
   `current_week`, it is honoured as a further lower bound (`max(current_week,
   actual_start_week)`). **Consequence, stated plainly:** for most non-frozen projects in the actual
   46-project seed dataset (which are typically scheduled starting near `CURRENT_WEEK=31` with no
   `actual_start_week` hint), this will produce a systematic ~6-week-later start compared to the
   prototype oracle. This is an expected, `INTENTIONAL`-classified divergence for P2-T02/T03's
   `docs/ORACLE_DIVERGENCE.md`, not a `PORT_BUG` — but it is the single decision in this task most
   likely to generate a large volume of oracle-diff noise, and I want P2-T02/T03 and P2-T04
   specifically pointed at it rather than discovering it cold.
3. **Which chamber a *frozen* project's lab step is assigned to, when multiple chambers are
   eligible.** DOMAIN_RULES.md doesn't say. Prototype: `Q=I[0]`, "the first eligible chamber" in
   whatever order the input chamber array happens to be in. Resolved analogously but made
   caller-order-independent (see determinism note below): "first" here means first in a
   `chamber_id`-ascending-sorted candidate list, not first in `ScheduleInput.chambers`' supplied
   order.
4. **What happens when a project has no assigned leader at all
   (`ProjectInput.leader_engineer_id is None`, or it doesn't resolve to any `EngineerInput`).**
   DOMAIN_RULES.md's booking rules don't mention this case. Prototype: immediate `leftOut=true,
   noEngineer=true`, no steps attempted, `catMismatch` never evaluated (the early-continue happens
   before that check). Replicated exactly: `left_out=True, no_leader=True, cat_not_allowed=False,
   steps=()`.
5. **`within_year` for excluded (Commercialized/On Hold) projects.** DOMAIN_RULES.md's
   completing-within-year formula is stated for `!left_out` projects and is silent on excluded ones.
   Prototype: `Commercialized -> withinYear:true` (trivially "already done"), `On Hold ->
   withinYear:false`. Replicated: `within_year = (status == "Commercialized")` for every excluded
   project (covers On Hold, the P1-added "Draft" status, and any future/unrecognized status the same
   way — default to `False`, never assume success for an unknown case).
6. **Whether a `left_out` project retains the steps it successfully booked before hitting the
   infeasible step, or reports zero steps.** Invariant I5 ("complete 14-step schedule OR
   `LEFT_OUT=true`") doesn't say. Prototype keeps whatever partial `steps` array it built before
   `break`ing out of the per-step loop (already-consumed engineer/chamber capacity is never
   un-booked). Replicated this — `ProjectScheduleOutcome.steps` for a `left_out` project may be
   non-empty (a genuine partial schedule) and this is documented explicitly on the dataclass so a
   future reader doesn't assume `left_out => steps == ()`.
7. **Sort-tie / chamber-candidate-tie determinism strengthening — my own decision, not
   prototype-sourced, made for Invariant I8's "no set/order dependence" requirement specifically.**
   The prototype's project sort relies on JavaScript's guaranteed-stable `Array.sort` to preserve
   *caller-supplied array order* for ties across all four documented sort keys
   (frozen/priority/status/category); similarly its per-week chamber-candidate search
   (`I.find(...)`) walks eligible chambers in raw input-array order. Neither behaviour is something a
   pure function should derive determinism from, since nothing in `ScheduleInput`'s contract promises
   `projects`/`chambers` arrive in any particular order. **Decision:** added `project_id` as an
   explicit fifth, always-decisive sort key (never contradicts the documented four-key order — only
   breaks otherwise-arbitrary ties), and sort eligible chambers by `chamber_id` before searching, in
   both the frozen ("pick the first eligible one") and non-frozen ("search for headroom") lab-step
   paths. Verified this holds via `_selftest.py`'s `scenario_determinism`, which re-runs the same
   projects in reversed tuple order and asserts structurally-identical output.

### [2026-08-30 12:30] P2-T02 — algorithm-engineer (interrupted) + rpd-orchestrator (completed)

**Did:** algorithm-engineer wrote `tests/oracle/capture_oracle.cjs` in full — a well-reasoned,
thoroughly-documented script that directly `eval()`s the prototype's own unmodified scheduler
function (`qm`, sliced verbatim out of `reference/rpd-platform-prototype.html` using the same
marker-slicing technique P1-T03's `extract_prototype_data.cjs` established) against the real
P1-T03 seed dataset — but the agent session hit a usage limit immediately before actually running

**Files touched:** `tests/oracle/capture_oracle.cjs` (one-line fix — see Decisions),
`tests/oracle/oracle_output.json` (generated), `docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` (P2-T02 → DONE),
`docs/MEMORY.md` (this entry).

**Decisions:** The bug: `capture_oracle.cjs` opened with `"use strict";`, but the script's core
mechanism (documented at length in its own header comment) depends on a *direct* `eval()` call
leaking the extracted snippet's `var`/`function qm(...)` declarations into the enclosing function's
scope — the same mechanism `extract_prototype_data.cjs` (P1-T03) relies on, which has no
`"use strict"` directive. Strict mode gives direct eval its own private variable environment, so
under strict mode the declarations never leak out and `qm` is never bound where the script expects
it — confirmed by reproducing the exact `TypeError`-adjacent failure the interrupted agent would
have hit had it run the script. Fix: removed the `"use strict"` directive, replaced with a comment
explaining why its absence is deliberate (mirroring `extract_prototype_data.cjs`'s own precedent).
This is exactly the kind of bug that's invisible from reading the code alone — the script's own
docstring even correctly explains *why* direct eval was chosen over indirect eval for this exact
scope-leaking reason, but missed that its own top-level strict-mode directive silently defeated the
mechanism it was relying on. A reminder that "looks correct and is well-reasoned" is not the same
as "was actually run" — this is why P1's tasks were held to live verification, not just code review,
and why this task needed the same treatment despite the interruption.

Post-fix verification performed directly: ran the script twice, `diff`'d the two
`oracle_output.json` outputs — byte-identical, confirming the script's own "byte-reproducible"
claim is actually true, not just asserted. Confirmed `source.constants_read_from_prototype`
(`current_week=31, within_year_week=52, horizon_weeks=78`) matches `docs/DOMAIN_RULES.md`'s Horizon
constants exactly, read directly out of the evaluated prototype scope rather than hardcoded in the
script — good design, since it means the script would flag a mismatch itself if the prototype ever
changed rather than silently trusting stale values. Spot-checked project `26-00200` (category B):
its first three `PDD-A/B/C` steps each show `duration_weeks: 1`, matching `max(1, round(2 * 0.5)) =
1` from DOMAIN_RULES.md's formula for a 2-base-week design step at category B's 0.5 multiplier —
consistent, gives confidence the rest of the capture is trustworthy without hand-checking all 46
projects.

Output summary: 46 projects captured (matching P1-T03's actual seed count, not the aspirational
"~236" — consistent with that task's own resolution), 2 excluded (Commercialized/On Hold), 8
left_out. `scheduling_order` is deliberately NOT captured (the script's own header explains why:
`qm`'s internal walk order is never returned by the function, and exposing it would require editing

**Did:** Followed the Memory Protocol in full before writing code: re-read `docs/DOMAIN_RULES.md`
(Invariants section, verbatim wording), `docs/MEMORY.md` in full (BOOTSTRAP through P2-T03, with

Invariants I1–I10 against any `(ScheduleInput, ScheduleOutput)` pair — and
`backend/scheduling/_selftest_invariants.py`, an informal self-test (same pattern as P2-T01's
`_selftest.py`) verifying the validator in both directions the task required. Did not touch
`backend/models/`, `backend/api/`, `backend/seed/`, `tests/oracle/`, `docs/ORACLE_DIVERGENCE.md`, or

and accepted).

**Files touched (all new, both under `backend/scheduling/`):**
- `backend/scheduling/invariants.py` — the validator.
- `backend/scheduling/_selftest_invariants.py` — the two-direction self-test (run via
  `python -m scheduling._selftest_invariants` from `backend/`).
- `backend/scheduling/__init__.py` — extended the package's public `__all__` surface with
  `InvariantViolation`, `validate_invariants`, `check_scheduler_determinism`,
  `compute_design_load_by_hub`, `compute_lab_load_by_hub` (added imports from the new
  `scheduling.invariants` module alongside the existing `scheduling.greedy`/`scheduling.types`

**Design:**

`InvariantViolation` (`@dataclass(frozen=True)`): `invariant: str` (always one of the literal
strings `"I1"`.."I10"`), `description: str` (self-contained human-readable explanation), and six
optional context fields (`project_id`, `step_id`, `engineer_id`, `chamber_id`, `hub`, `week`, all
`| None = None`) — only the fields relevant to a given violation are populated, never fabricated.

`validate_invariants(schedule_input: ScheduleInput, schedule_output: ScheduleOutput, *,
check_determinism: bool = True) -> tuple[InvariantViolation, ...]` — the main entry point. Runs all
ten checks unconditionally (never raises, never short-circuits on the first violation — an empty
tuple means all ten invariants hold), returning every violation found in one pass, in a fixed
I1→I10 order. `check_determinism=True` by default so a single call covers the full permanent
correctness contract; settable to `False` when a caller (e.g. this module's own Direction 2 self-test,
validating many different hand-crafted-broken `ScheduleOutput`s against the same `ScheduleInput`) wants
to skip the extra `run_greedy_sgs` re-runs I8's check performs internally.

`check_scheduler_determinism(schedule_input: ScheduleInput, *, runs: int = 2) ->
tuple[InvariantViolation, ...]` — I8's check, deliberately exposed as its own top-level reusable
function (not just an internal helper folded into `validate_invariants`), per the task's explicit
instruction that it be "a reusable, general-purpose version any caller can invoke on any
ScheduleInput, not just P2-T01's own hardcoded scenarios." Takes only a `ScheduleInput` — no
`ScheduleOutput` needed, since I8 is a property of the scheduler function itself, not of any one
output. Runs `run_greedy_sgs` `runs` times and asserts every run after the first is both
structurally equal (`==`) and byte-identical (`repr()`) to the first run, mirroring P2-T01's own
`_selftest.py::scenario_determinism` precedent for checking both.

`compute_design_load_by_hub`/`compute_lab_load_by_hub(schedule_input, schedule_output) -> dict[str,
int|float]` — also exposed as their own public functions (I6/I7's aggregates), not just inlined into
the corresponding checks, since a future Capacity-surface reporting layer (P3/P4, not yet built) is
very likely to want exactly these two aggregates and re-implementing them a second time would be
exactly the drift risk `domain_constants.py`'s own docstring warns against.

**Per-invariant implementation notes (only where the check required a judgement call beyond a literal
reading of DOMAIN_RULES.md's Invariants section text):**

- **I1/I2** (engineer/chamber conflicts): built as pairwise/per-(resource,week) overlap detection
  independent of anything `ScheduleOutput` itself claims via `eng_conflict`/`overlap` — i.e. the
  validator recomputes whether an actual conflict exists from raw `StepSchedule` start/end weeks,
  then checks the flag is set consistently with that recomputation (both directions: an actual
  conflict between two non-frozen projects is *itself* a violation, since that should structurally
  never happen; an actual conflict involving a frozen project requires the flag to be raised on at
  least one side). This "never trust the aggregate, recompute from primitives" approach directly
  follows the design intent P2-T01's own MEMORY.md entry stated for `StepSchedule`'s raw fields
  ("so P2-T04's validator can independently recompute I1/I2/I6/I7 from first principles instead of
  trusting anything this module aggregates").
- **I5**: read "every scheduled project" as "every non-`excluded` outcome" (an `excluded` project,
  per DOMAIN_RULES.md, was never fed into the greedy walk at all — P2-T01's own `excluded` vs.
  `left_out` distinction makes this unambiguous). Added the converse direction too (`left_out=True`
  with a *complete* step count is also flagged) since a "complete OR left_out" invariant would be
  meaningless if both could be simultaneously true — this direction is not literally stated in
  DOMAIN_RULES.md's I5 text but follows necessarily from the "OR" being a real disjunction, and
  P2-T01's own scheduler never produces this combination by construction, so it costs nothing to
  check.
- **I6/I7 — explicit N/A-for-now scoping, per this task's own brief:** DOMAIN_RULES.md's literal I6/I7
  text says these totals "must reconcile with the Capacity surface." No such surface exists yet — P3
  (API layer) and P4 (Capacity Planning UI) have not started. `_check_i6_design_load_computable`/
  `_check_i7_lab_load_computable` validate everything checkable at the pure-function level today:
  (a) no negative/malformed step durations (would make the aggregate meaningless), and (b) internal
  consistency — the per-hub breakdown (`compute_design_load_by_hub`/`compute_lab_load_by_hub`) sums to
  exactly the same grand total as an independently-sourced second loop (iterating
  `schedule_input.projects` and looking up each project's outcome, rather than iterating
  `schedule_output.project_outcomes` directly) computes on its own. This is explicitly **not** a check
  against a live Capacity surface — there is nothing yet to reconcile against. Recording this
  explicitly here (not silently skipping the reconciliation half): when P3/P4 build the Capacity
  surface, a *new* check (comparing `compute_design_load_by_hub`'s output against that surface's
  reported figures) will need to be added on top of what exists here — this validator's I6/I7 checks
  will remain correct and useful as a component of that larger check, not replaced by it.
- **I9**: re-derives `within_year` from the same formula DOMAIN_RULES.md states
  (`!left_out AND (last_step_end + delay <= WITHIN_YEAR_WEEK)`), plus the excluded-project resolution
  P2-T01's MEMORY.md entry recorded (`within_year = status == "Commercialized"` for excluded projects,
  since DOMAIN_RULES.md is silent on excluded projects specifically and this is what was already
  reviewed and accepted for the scheduler's own output) — deliberately re-applying the *same*
  resolution here rather than inventing an independent/stricter reading, since the validator's job is
  to check the accepted contract is honoured, not to silently redefine it. Also cross-checks
  `spillover`'s consistency with the same re-derivation as a closely-related corollary (DOMAIN_RULES.md
  defines SPILLOVER as the within-year formula's negation).
- **I10**: scoped per this task's explicit framing — no "apply priorities" action exists yet at the

  frozen-only sub-input, and their resource consumption is fed into the model as fixed background
  occupancy the non-frozen projects route around. Agreed this is provably equivalent to the
  frozen-project subset of a full greedy run: greedy's sort key places every frozen project before
  every non-frozen one, and a frozen project's booking never depends on a later-processed project.
  The two infeasibility traps the design avoids (engineer background collapsed to a per-week *set*
  before deriving disjoint intervals; chamber background capped at `max_concurrent` per week) are
  both correct and necessary — a frozen ENG_CONFLICT or OVERLAP is a DOMAIN_RULES.md *warning*, and
  a hard CP-SAT constraint has no "flag and continue", so the conflict must never reach the solver.
  Self-test confirms both paths stay FEASIBLE end-to-end.
- **I3 (sequential steps):** `model.Add(start >= prev_end)` between consecutive steps. Correct.
- **I4 (lab step → eligible chamber only):** per-candidate-chamber optional intervals over
  `{c : c.lab_region == region and step.step_id in c.allowed_stages}`, `sum(assign_vars) == present`.
  Correct; zero-eligible-chamber case is pre-resolved to LEFT_OUT before the model is built.
- **I5 (fully scheduled OR left_out):** single shared per-project `present` literal gates every
  step's interval and the chamber-assignment sum. CP-SAT deliberately targets I5's clean reading
  (no partial-step retention on LEFT_OUT) rather than replicating greedy's partial-retention quirk —
  agreed this is the better reading and was an explicit instruction to that task; it will show up as
  an INTENTIONAL greedy-vs-CP-SAT difference in P2-T07, not a bug.

  identical rule to greedy's non-frozen path (P2-T01's earliest-start-floor resolution). Consistent.

  but defines no number — priority is a *band* and a sort key, never a scalar, and `ProjectInput`
  carries neither the 13-dim weighted score nor any financial value. The module fills this with an
  ordinal band weight `{P1:4,P2:3,P3:2,P4:1,Q:0}` mirroring greedy's own sort precedence, plus a
  scaled-coarse `present`-count tie-break. This is a real gap-fill, not a silent invention →
  **ADR 0005 written.** The `INFEASIBLE → RuntimeError` guard is correct: every decision project has
  an always-valid "absent" fallback, so INFEASIBLE would be a modelling bug, not a domain outcome.

  defect. Acceptable for P2-T06; P2-T07/T09 should keep using `num_search_workers=1`.

- **ADR 0004 (delay is a terminal adjustment, not propagated):** respected. Perturbed `delay_weeks`
  is passed into the per-iteration `ScheduleInput` (where greedy uses it only for the
  within-year/spillover check, never to shift step dates) AND separately added to `end_week` to form
  the completion-week sample. No propagation into step start/end. The `iterations=1` cross-check
  proves it: unperturbed completion week == `end_week + delay_weeks` exactly, and delay-only
  perturbation leaves every project's `end_week` unchanged (completion only ever moves later).
- **Determinism (I8, extended to the forecaster):** a single `random.Random(seed)` is threaded
  through the whole run; no module-level `random.`, no numpy, no global RNG. Per-iteration draw
  order is fixed: one triangular duration-factor draw first (only when `duration_perturbation`),
  then per-project Poisson delay draws in `project_id`-sorted order; `_poisson` (Knuth) consumes
  only `rng.random()`. `_nearest_rank` and the dict accumulation iterate in sorted / fixed order.
  Self-test confirms byte-identical (`==` on frozen all-tuple dataclasses) re-runs and
  input-order independence. CP-SAT inner solver (`solver="cp_sat"`) is only "empirically
  deterministic" per `cp_sat.py`'s own documented caveat — greedy is the default and recommended
  inner solver; this matches the P2-T06 review's treatment of I8.

**Decisions (perturbation-model gap-fills — `docs/DOMAIN_RULES.md` is silent on ALL of the
following; P2-T08's acceptance criteria only says "P50/P80 completion-week distributions per project
from repeated solver runs under input perturbation; deterministic given a fixed random seed"):**

1. **Inner solver = greedy by default** (`run_greedy_sgs`, ~2 ms/solve on the 46-project dataset,
   exactly deterministic per I8). `solver="cp_sat"` is available but ~1.8 s/solve → a 500-iteration
   run would take ~15 min and only be empirically deterministic. The forecaster is solver-agnostic
   via a `solver=` argument.
2. **Two independent perturbation dimensions, both on by default, each fully parameterised by
   function arguments with documented defaults:**
   a. **Per-project additive delay** — extra weeks ~ `Poisson(λ_i)` with
      `λ_i = delay_lambda_base + delay_lambda_per_current_week × max(0, project.delay_weeks)`
      (defaults `1.0` and `0.5`). Rationale: Poisson is the natural non-negative-integer
      "count of extra weeks" law with one parameter per project; projects already flagged late
      (non-zero `delay_weeks`) slip more in expectation. Applied via ADR 0004's terminal channel,
      so it moves completion weeks without destabilising schedule structure.
   b. **Per-iteration global multiplicative factor on every workflow step's `base_weeks`**, drawn
      from `Triangular(low=0.85, high=1.30, mode=1.0)` (the classic PERT / three-point
      project-estimate distribution, deliberately right-skewed — overruns more likely than
      underruns). Re-rounded to `max(1, round(base_weeks × factor))`; the category multiplier +
      `max(1, round(...))` in `duration_weeks` is then applied downstream by the solver as usual.
      This is the dimension that makes contention — and therefore `left_out` / `spillover` —
      actually vary across iterations; delay perturbation alone never changes feasibility.
   A real client-calibrated model replaces exactly those defaults, or is bypassed entirely by
   setting both `*_perturbation=False` and pre-perturbing inputs upstream.
3. **Iteration count: default 500** (`DEFAULT_ITERATIONS`). Greedy inner solver → ~1–2 s wall clock
   for the full 500-iteration run on the 46-project dataset. Overridable via `iterations=`.
4. **Percentile method: nearest-rank, no interpolation.** For percentile `p` over `N` ascending-
   sorted samples: `rank = ceil(p/100 × N)`, 1-indexed, clamped to `[1, N]`; return
   `sorted_values[rank-1]`. `N == 0 → None`. Chosen over `statistics.quantiles` / numpy percentile
   defaults because it is trivially reproducible, library-independent, and always returns an actual
   observed completion week (an integer that really occurred), which is the right semantics for
   "the week by which 80% of simulated futures have this project done".
5. **"Completion week" for one iteration:**
   - fully-scheduled project → `last_step_end_week + perturbed_delay_weeks` (identical to the input
     of greedy's own within-year formula);
   - `left_out` that iteration → no sample (excluded from that project's percentile computation),
     counted in `iterations_left_out`;
   - `excluded` project (Commercialized / On Hold / Draft / any non-schedulable status) → never
     forecast: `excluded=True`, percentiles `None`, zero samples; `within_year_frequency` mirrors
     the solver (1.0 iff the solver marks it within-year, e.g. Commercialized).
   Per-project frequencies are fractions of *all* `iterations` (not of the scheduled subset), so
   `left_out_frequency + within_year_frequency` need not sum to 1 — a project can be
   scheduled-but-spillover in the remaining iterations.
6. **Portfolio `within_year_count_per_iteration`** is the per-iteration count of within-year
   projects (including excluded-but-within-year, e.g. Commercialized, to mirror the solver),
   summarised with the same nearest-rank method into `p50_within_year_count` /
   `p80_within_year_count`. P80 is the optimistic tail (80% of simulated futures deliver this many
   or fewer within-year).
7. **`DeliveryForecast` / `ProjectDeliveryForecast` / `PerturbationParams` are frozen dataclasses
   with all-tuple collection fields**, so value-equality is byte-identity of the serialised form —
   this is how the determinism self-test asserts I8 for the forecaster.

**Broke / discovered (this is the substantial part of this entry — a coordinator review caught two

1. **`pnpm typecheck` was failing — 9 errors, all `Property 'toHaveTextContent'/'toHaveClass' does
   not exist on type 'Assertion<HTMLElement>'` in the theme test.** Root cause: `src/test/setup.ts`
   imported `@testing-library/jest-dom/matchers` and called `expect.extend(matchers)` by hand — this
   registers the matchers at runtime (so `pnpm test` would have silently passed) but does **not**
   pull in `@testing-library/jest-dom`'s `declare module 'vitest' { interface Assertion ... }` type
   augmentation, which only ships from the package's separate `/vitest` entry point (confirmed by
   reading `node_modules/@testing-library/jest-dom/types/vitest.d.ts` directly — it does the
   `declare module` merge — versus `/matchers`, whose types are matcher-shape-only). Fix: replaced
   the manual `expect.extend` with a single `import '@testing-library/jest-dom/vitest'` (which does
   both the runtime `expect.extend` call — confirmed by reading `dist/vitest.mjs` — and the type
   augmentation) in `src/test/setup.ts`. `pnpm typecheck` is clean after this change alone; no other
   code needed to change.
2. **`pnpm test` was crashing the entire runner before any test executed** —
   `TypeError: webidl.util.markAsUncloneable is not a function` thrown from inside `undici` while
   `jsdom` loaded, not a test failure. Root cause, confirmed by reading the installed packages'
   `package.json` `engines` fields directly rather than guessing: the pre-existing pin
   `"jsdom": "30.0.1"` requires Node `^22.22.2 || ^24.15.0 || >=26.0.0`, and its bundled `undici@^8.9.0`
   separately requires Node `>=22.19.0` — this environment runs Node `v20.20.2`, which satisfies
   neither. This is a genuine toolchain/environment mismatch in what the prior (unlogged) session
   pinned, not something introduced in this session. Fix: downgraded `jsdom` to `29.1.1` in
   `package.json` (`undici@^7.25.0`, which only requires Node `>=20.18.1` — satisfied) and re-ran
   `pnpm install`. Verified this is safe, not just convenient: `vitest@4.1.11`'s own
   `peerDependencies`/`peerDependenciesMeta` declare `jsdom: "*"` as an **optional** peer (checked
   the installed `vitest/package.json` directly) — Vitest does not pin a minimum jsdom version, so
   this is a legitimate compatible-version choice, not a workaround masking a real incompatibility.
   Documented the reasoning (with the exact error and the version-compatibility chain) in
   `frontend/README.md`'s Testing section so a future session doesn't "helpfully" bump jsdom back to
   `30.x` and reintroduce the crash, and flagged there that it should be revisited once the target
   Node runtime moves to 22+.
3. Two TypeScript errors surfaced only once real code exercised them (not defects in prior work,
   just things that had no code path to trigger them until this session): (a) `React.lazy(() =>
   import('lottie-react'))` doesn't type-check directly against `lottie-react`'s real shape (no
   default export) — resolved by mapping to `{ default: mod.Lottie }` in the lazy loader, discovered
   via decision #3 above; (b) a class-field override (`state`) on `ErrorBoundary` needed an explicit
   `override` modifier under this repo's `noImplicitOverride: true` — one-line fix.

**Adjudication of the two carry-forward flags:**

**(a) CP-SAT drops schedulable P1 `26-00201` entirely under ADR 0005.** Independently re-ran
`run_cp_sat` and confirmed directly: `26-00201` (P1, category A, hub PD-India, customer Coca-Cola,
`gates=["Customer certification at risk (Coke/Pepsi)"]` — one of DOMAIN_RULES.md's three hard-gate
reasons that force P1) comes back `left_out=True, steps=()` under CP-SAT. Under greedy, the same
project is scheduled (all 14 steps booked, `spillover=True`, completing week 58 — 6 weeks past
`WITHIN_YEAR_WEEK=52`). Confirmed this is a genuine, correctly-modelled consequence of ADR 0005's
objective as written: because the project completes at week 58 under *either* solver's own
resource-contention profile, `band_weight × within_year` scores exactly 0 whether CP-SAT schedules it
or not, so the coarse present-over-absent tie-break (which only fires on an actual tie) never
protects it — CP-SAT correctly identifies that reclaiming its capacity lifts three *other* projects
across the within-year line (11→14), a strict net gain under the stated objective, not a tie. This is
not a `PORT_BUG`, not an invariant violation (0 violations either side), and not a misapplication of
ADR 0005 — it is ADR 0005 working exactly as specified.
**My position:** this does **not** block the P2 gate. P2's gate criteria (per `docs/
IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`) are about the scheduling engine correctly implementing DOMAIN_RULES.md and
its ADRs, invariants holding, and divergences being classified — all satisfied here. ADR 0005 itself
already documents this exact class of outcome as a known, provisional consequence and explicitly
flags it for client resolution before a real value scheme replaces the ordinal weights. However, I
do **not** consider this settled for production: a CP-SAT run that silently produces zero scheduled
steps for a customer-certification-at-risk P1 (as opposed to greedy's outcome, which at least shows
the project progressing, just late) is a materially different and more concerning UX than "scheduled
but late," and must not go live in the Capacity Planning "Auto-assign" feature (P4-T07, which is the
first place a CP-SAT-optimized schedule would reach an actual user) without an explicit client
decision. **Recommendation to the orchestrator:** open a new numbered question in `docs/
OPEN_QUESTIONS.md` (this repo currently has none covering the CP-SAT objective's project-selection
behavior) capturing this exact scenario, and treat it as a blocking prerequisite for P4-T07
specifically (not for the P2 gate) — whichever way the client answers, ADR 0005 is superseded by a
new ADR at that point per its own stated consequences, exactly as P2-T07's review already recommended
options for (secondary objective term rewarding P1s even in spillover, or a hard/soft constraint that
frozen/P1 projects are always scheduled when feasible).

**(b) Monte Carlo perturbation defaults (Poisson delay, Triangular duration, 500 iterations) are
provisional; DOMAIN_RULES.md is silent.** Agree with the prior reviews' assessment: this is a
reporting/forecasting overlay layered on top of the deterministic scheduling contract, not part of
Invariants I1-I10 (none of which mention Monte Carlo, forecasting, or percentiles — confirmed via
`grep -niE "monte|p50|p80|forecast|percentile|perturb" docs/DOMAIN_RULES.md`, zero hits, same check
the P2-T08 review already ran and I re-ran myself). Every perturbation parameter is a documented
function-argument default, the whole model is bypassable (`*_perturbation=False` + pre-perturbed
inputs), and determinism under a fixed seed is real (independently re-verified above, not just
self-tested). **My position:** acceptable as-is for the P2 gate — this is not a scheduler-correctness
question and does not need an ADR (ADRs in this project are reserved for DOMAIN_RULES.md-scoped
scheduling contract decisions, not every parameterized reporting default). It should be labeled in
the UI, once a forecasting surface exists, as a provisional model pending client calibration
(P4/P5 concern, not P2's).

**Deviations from plan:** none from P2-T10's acceptance criteria (independent re-derivation, I1-I10
assertion, ORACLE_DIVERGENCE.md classification check, `tests/oracle/` deletion check, gate
