  scoped to the one place a write-permitted user is actively editing them.
- `ProjectFormDialog`'s single form component serves both create (`POST`) and edit (`PATCH`); the
  edit path always sends a full-form snapshot (every field, not a sparse diff) — so a user clearing a
  field back to blank actually nulls it out server-side, consistent with the backend's
  `exclude_unset` PATCH semantics (every key present in the JSON body counts as an explicit set).
- No Recharts/ECharts/Lottie/three.js in this surface — it's forms + a virtualized list, nothing
  chart-shaped. `RegistrationPage` is its own lazy route chunk (6.87 KB gzip), not in the initial

- `useProjectList` fetches with `limit=500` (same convention P4-T05's Gantt used) — no truncation
  notice added, since `GET /projects` returns a plain array with no `total_count` metadata to key one

existing security-auditor precedent drawing the identical line eight days prior in this same

### [2026-09-01] P4-T10 — workflow-auditor: Dashboard/Capacity/Matrix/Gantt reconciliation

**Did:** Performed the P4-T10 workflow-auditor half of the P4 gate — cross-surface reconciliation
of Dashboard/Capacity/Matrix/Gantt against a single live `ScheduleRun` source, Invariant I9 traced
end-to-end, and adjudicated the two carry-forward flags from the P4-T02/T03/T05 reviews. **Result:
PASS** for the scope of this task (see caveat on the overall P4 gate at the end).

**Method (live, not just code review):** Read `docs/DOMAIN_RULES.md`, this file, and
`IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`'s P4 section (including every P4-T01..T06 review entry) first. Then read
`backend/api/routers/{dashboard,capacity,gantt,priorities,schedule_runs}.py` in full, and every
non-test file under `frontend/src/surfaces/{dashboard,capacity,gantt,matrix}/`. Then, rather than
relying on static reading alone, built a standalone script
(`/private/tmp/.../scratchpad/live_trace.py`, ephemeral, not committed) that: spins up a real
ephemeral Postgres via `testcontainers`, runs the real `alembic upgrade head`, seeds the real
46-project demo dataset + currency rates via the real `seed/` scripts, then drives the REAL FastAPI
app in-process over `httpx.AsyncClient(ASGITransport(app=app))` — creating a real provisioned `User`
row + RBAC `Role`/`UserRole` rows and overriding only `get_current_principal`/`get_db` (the same
override points `tests/auth_helpers.py` uses) so every request exercises the real RBAC/hub-scope
code, not a mock. Called the real `POST /schedule-runs/greedy-recalc` as Admin (creating + activating
a real `ScheduleRun`), then queried `GET /schedule-runs/active`, `GET
/dashboard/completing-within-year`, `GET /capacity/hub-load`, `GET /capacity/class-breakdown`, `GET
/gantt?limit=500`, `GET /priorities`, `GET /priorities/summary`, `GET /dashboard/pipeline-totals`,
`GET /dashboard/status-overview` — both as an unrestricted Admin and as a `Hub Planner` scoped to one
hub (`hub_scope_all=False`) — and cross-checked every number by hand. Ran the whole trace twice,
against two independently fresh-seeded databases, to also probe run-to-run reproducibility.

**Findings — cross-surface reconciliation (PASS):**
1. Dashboard's `within_year_count`/`spillover_count`/`left_out_count` exactly matched a manual count
   of its own `rows` array (sanity) — and the exact SETS of project ids flagged `left_out` /
   `spillover` / `cat_not_allowed` matched byte-for-byte between Dashboard and Gantt (two separately
   implemented routers reading the same `ScheduleRunProjectOutcome` snapshot rows independently).
2. Capacity's `/class-breakdown` total `left_out_count` (summed across the 4 category rows) exactly
   equalled Dashboard's `left_out_count`.
3. All four schedule-run-backed responses (`schedule-runs/active`, `dashboard`, `capacity/hub-load`,
   `capacity/class-breakdown`, `gantt`) reported the identical `schedule_run_version` for the one
   active run, every time.
4. Capacity's server-computed per-hub `design_load_weeks`/`lab_load_units` (Invariants I6/I7) matched,
   to the exact decimal, an INDEPENDENT recomputation I performed by summing `duration_weeks`
   (design) / `duration_weeks × 0.5` (lab) straight off Gantt's own per-step rows for the same run,
   for all 6 hubs, in both trial runs. This verifies I6/I7 end-to-end across the real API boundary,
   not just inside `scheduling/`'s own unit tests.
5. Hub-scoping is consistent across surfaces: a `Hub Planner` principal scoped to one hub (PD-India)
   saw `dashboard.within_year_count` for that hub exactly equal to the portfolio-wide dashboard
   response filtered to that hub's rows (5 == 5); Gantt's hub-scoped rows all belonged to that one hub
   (20/20); Capacity `/hub-load` returned exactly one row, for that hub.
6. `GET /priorities` / `GET /priorities/summary` (Matrix) carry ZERO schedule-run-derived fields —
   grep-confirmed no `schedule_run_version`/`within_year`/`spillover`/`left_out` anywhere in the

7. Spot-checked the deliberate "two senses of 'spillover'" terminology risk

   completing between the two fetches) the version *label* could theoretically show a newer number
   than what the figures below it actually reflect. Never observed in this trace; purely theoretical.
   The already-planned backend addition of `solver_type`/`computed_at` directly onto the primary
   response (eliminating the second call entirely) would also close this residual — not required to
   pass this gate, but worth folding into that same follow-up ticket.

**New observation, flagged for the record only — NOT a P4-T10 finding, out of this task's scope and
authority:** Running the live trace twice, against two independently fresh-seeded copies of "the
same" 46-project dataset, produced different-but-internally-consistent outcome splits (run 1:
within_year=12/spillover=23/left_out=10; run 2: within_year=11/spillover=24/left_out=10 — `left_out`
identical both times; one marginal project moved between within-year and spillover, and PD-India's
`lab_load_units` shifted from 49.5 to 48.5 accordingly, consistently between Capacity and Gantt in
each run). Traced the cause: `backend/scheduling/greedy.py::_sort_key` uses `project.project_id` as
an explicit fifth tie-break beyond DOMAIN_RULES.md's four documented sort keys (frozen desc,
priority, status, category) — already reviewed and accepted at P2-T01 ("[2026-08-30 12:00] P2-T01
review") as a valid pure-function-determinism strengthening. Because `Project.id` is a randomly
generated UUID assigned fresh by `seed_demo_data.py` on every reseed (not the stable,
business-meaningful `external_code`), two projects that tie on all four DOMAIN_RULES.md-specified
keys get a different, effectively-random tie-break resolution across reseeds/reimports of otherwise
-identical portfolio data — moving which one of several equally-ranked, marginal projects lands
within-year vs. spillover, with zero change to any documented business attribute. This does **not**
violate Invariant I8 as literally worded (I8 is pure-function determinism given one fixed
`ScheduleInput`, which holds — `run_greedy_sgs` has no randomness and a stable sort with an explicit
tiebreak) and it does **not** contradict any P4-T10 cross-surface finding above (every surface
remained fully internally consistent with every other surface within each of the two runs
individually). It is a real, previously-unflagged-from-this-angle business-reproducibility
sensitivity to a non-business, DB-surrogate key: a real-world re-import of the same portfolio next
planning cycle could silently reshuffle which marginal project makes the within-year cut, with no
change to any project's priority/status/category/frozen state. Recommending a backlog item (not a
P4-T10 blocker, and not something this role has authority to fix or gate on its own, since P2 already
closed and the scheduling package belongs to algorithm-engineer) — tie-break on `Project.external_code`
instead of `Project.id`, or explicitly document in `DOMAIN_RULES.md` that ties are resolved by an
internal, reseed-sensitive key. Flagged here for orchestrator routing, not actioned by this task.

**Verdict: PASS** for the P4-T10 workflow-auditor scope — Dashboard/Capacity/Gantt numbers reconcile
exactly against a single live `ScheduleRun` source (within-year count, per-hub load, per-project
outcome flags), Matrix is correctly out-of-scope for those numbers, and Invariant I9 holds
end-to-end, live-traced from the backend snapshot through to what each surface's own hooks/components
actually bind and render (not merely asserted in each surface's own prior individual review). Both

**What "Apply Logic" turned out to mean — investigated, not guessed, but still an interpretation,
flagged for orchestrator confirmation:** `docs/PROJECT_AND_STACK.md` §2 says Capacity Planning has
"An 'Apply Logic' action and an 'Auto-assign' action for bulk resource assignment." No backend
endpoint is named "apply logic" anywhere — `backend/api/routers/engineers.py` and `chambers.py`'s own
module docstrings explicitly disclaim it ("'Apply Logic' / 'Auto-assign' are explicitly OUT OF SCOPE
... there is no 'apply logic' endpoint at all yet"). `backend/api/routers/schedule_runs.py`'s module
docstring explicitly disclaims being "Apply Priorities" (Matrix's band-recompute) and "Auto-assign"
(the CP-SAT path) by name, but does **not** disclaim being used as "Apply Logic." Reading
`docs/PROJECT_AND_STACK.md` §2 literally — two named actions, both "for bulk resource assignment,"
differing only in which algorithm decides — "Logic" reads as the deterministic, rule-based greedy SGS
scheduler (`docs/DOMAIN_RULES.md`'s booking rules, applied verbatim), and "Auto-assign" reads as the
autonomous CP-SAT optimizer. This is also the only reading consistent with why OQ#10 blocks
Auto-assign specifically and not this action: OQ#10 is a CP-SAT-only failure mode. On this reading,
"Apply Logic" is wired to the existing `POST /schedule-runs/greedy-recalc` primitive (Admin-only,
synchronous, activates a new whole-portfolio schedule). **This is flagged loudly in
`components/apply-logic-panel.tsx`'s own module docstring as an interpretation of an undocumented
term, not a confirmed contract** — if backend-builder or the orchestrator intended something else
(e.g. a still-to-be-built dedicated endpoint), this wiring should be revisited rather than treated as
settled precedent.

**Backend contract gaps found (flagged, not fixed — backend is not this role's to write):**

### [2026-09-01] P4-T06 remediation — build/typecheck/test regressions — frontend-builder

**Task:** narrow, mechanical remediation of two real regressions the orchestrator found in
`frontend/` on re-verification of the already-DONE P4-T06 Project Registration surface, plus a
factual mtime check for undisclosed edits. Read `docs/DOMAIN_RULES.md`/`docs/MEMORY.md` per the
Memory Protocol; did not re-audit P4-T06's full scope (not requested, not needed for a two-line
test fix).

**Bug 1 — `pnpm typecheck`/`pnpm build` failing (TS2769), `components/project-form.test.tsx`:**
lines 149 and 155 called `screen.findByRole('option', { name: 'A', exact: true })` and
`{ name: 'P1', exact: true }`. `exact` is not a member of Testing Library's `ByRoleOptions` type
(it only exists on the text/label-matcher option types like `getByText`/`getByLabelText`); role
queries don't accept it. Since `'A'`/`'P1'` are already plain strings (exact match is the default
for string matchers regardless), the fix was simply deleting `, exact: true` from both object
literals, leaving `{ name: 'A' }` and `{ name: 'P1' }`. No other line in the file was touched.

**Bug 2 — failing test, `components/hard-gate-panel.test.tsx`, `'shows a loading skeleton while the
hard-gate status is pending'`:** the assertion `container.querySelector('[class*="animate-pulse"],
[data-slot="skeleton"]')` was written against shadcn's *stock* Skeleton conventions
(`animate-pulse`, `data-slot="skeleton"`), which this repo does not use. Read
`frontend/src/components/ui/skeleton.tsx` directly (left untouched, confirmed correct and used
elsewhere) — this repo's hand-rolled `Skeleton` renders `role="status"` + `aria-live="polite"` +
`aria-busy="true"` and a `before:animate-shimmer` Tailwind class, no `data-slot` attribute, no
`animate-pulse` class. Confirmed via `hard-gate-panel.tsx` (grep) that exactly one `<Skeleton>` is

Root-caused: Testing Library's `findBy*`/`waitFor` helpers have their own internal 1000ms
`asyncUtilTimeout`, independent of Vitest's (much larger) `testTimeout` — under full
file-parallelism (`vitest run`, no `--no-file-parallelism`), CPU contention across ~80
concurrently-transforming test files occasionally pushes a `findByRole` crossing a
`React.lazy`-chunk boundary, or a long `userEvent` sequence, past 1000ms. Not a real hang, not a
broken assertion — reproducible flakiness, not determinism. **Fixed** (test-infra only, in scope
for this role — no application/component code touched): added `configure({ asyncUtilTimeout:
5_000 })` (from `@testing-library/react`) to `frontend/src/test/setup.ts`, and `testTimeout:
10_000` to `vite.config.ts`'s `test` block for headroom. Re-verified: **4/4 clean unscoped `pnpm
test` runs after the fix** (295 tests / 81 files, 0 failures, every run). `pnpm typecheck` and
`pnpm lint` both re-ran clean (lint: 0 errors, 1 pre-existing `react-hooks/incompatible-library`
warning, unchanged).

**5. Axe accessibility pass — result: FAIL on all six surfaces. Real, reproducible violations, not
test bugs or flakiness** (structured JSON extracted from the actual `axe-core` output, not
eyeballed):

| Surface | Total instances | Breakdown |
|---|---|---|
| Dashboard | 46 | `color-contrast` serious ×42, `definition-list` serious ×2, `scrollable-region-focusable` serious ×2 |
| Capacity | 86 | `color-contrast` serious ×85, `scrollable-region-focusable` serious ×1 |
| Matrix | 20 | `color-contrast` serious ×20 |
| Gantt/Timeline | 7 | `color-contrast` serious ×7 |
| Registration | 42 | **`aria-required-children` CRITICAL ×23**, `color-contrast` serious ×19 |
| Planning | 10 | `color-contrast` serious ×10 |

Root causes, read directly from the violation `nodes[].html`/`data` (not just the rule id):
- **Global, cross-cutting `color-contrast` defect present on every single surface**: the app
  shell's `AppHeader` "Frigoglass" wordmark span (`className="ml-2 font-normal text-text-subtle"`)
  renders at **2.72:1** contrast (`#8e9eb4` on `#ffffff`) against WCAG AA's required 4.5:1 for
  normal-weight 14px text. This is a **design-token-level defect** (the `--color-text-subtle`
  semantic token itself, `src/styles/tokens.css`), not a per-surface bug — it appears on every
  page because the header is part of the always-rendered app shell. The bulk of each surface's
  remaining `color-contrast` count is the same `text-text-subtle`/`text-text-muted` family reused
  at 2xs (11px) on `ProjectStatusBadge`/stat captions/panel descriptions (e.g. the "In Queue"
  status pill measured at 4.14:1, just under threshold) — same token family, not a separate bug
  per instance.
- **Registration's CRITICAL `aria-required-children` (23 instances)**: `project-list.tsx`'s
  virtualized rows use `role="row"` on plain `<div>`s whose children are plain `<div>`/
  `<button aria-label>` elements instead of `role="cell"`/`"gridcell"` — an invalid ARIA
  row/cell structure (axe: "Required ARIA children role not present: cell, columnheader,
  gridcell, rowheader" / "Element has children which are not allowed"). Matrix/Gantt's own
  virtualized lists did **not** trigger this rule — confirmed only Registration's row markup uses
  literal `role="row"` without a matching cell role.
- **Dashboard's `definition-list` (2 instances)**: two `<dl>` elements (`aria-label="Pipeline
  composition..."` and one under `.border-t`) whose direct children are not exclusively
  `<dt>`/`<dd>`/`<script>`/`<template>`/`<div>` pairs.
- **`scrollable-region-focusable` (Capacity ×1, Dashboard ×2)**: virtualized table containers
  (`data-testid="virtual-table-scroll"`, `overflow-auto`) have no `tabindex`, so a keyboard-only
  user cannot scroll them.

**These are real component/design-system bugs, not fixed by this task.** Per this role's mandate
("you do not write feature code") and CLAUDE.md's Delegation Rule, fixing a shared semantic
design token (`text-text-subtle`) or a virtualized list's ARIA row/cell structure is
frontend-builder's territory, not qa-inspector's — flagged here with full reproduction detail
(rule id, exact contrast numbers, exact selectors) for routing, not silently worked around or
left as a bare "axe failed."

clean, reproducible Playwright run — flagged, not fixed, for the same "out of my remit" reason as
§5): `registration.spec.ts`'s own flow test — exercising the *real* product, not a test bug —

actual_start_week, tcogs, selling_price, gross_margin), and submits it out of Draft into

### [2026-09-01] P4-T11 — accessibility remediation — frontend-builder

**Task:** Remediate exactly the four axe finding classes from the P4-T09 qa-inspector FAIL (see
that entry, "[2026-09-01] P4-T09 — qa-inspector" §5), scoped narrowly per
`docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`'s P4-T11 entry. Read `docs/DOMAIN_RULES.md`, the full P4-T09 entry,
and the P4-T11 plan entry first, per the Memory Protocol. `backend/` was not touched (confirmed via
`find backend -newer docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`, excluding `__pycache__`/`.venv`: only a
pre-existing, untouched `backend/.env` and normal `__pycache__` bytecode churn from running
`alembic`/seed scripts show up — no source file was written).

**Note on continuity:** this session picked up mid-task after a tool/stream watchdog stall. At the
resume point, only `bar-chart.tsx` and `project-list.tsx` had been changed on disk; findings 1
(color-contrast) and 4 (scrollable-region-focusable) were still outstanding and are completed in
this entry, along with two additional fixes findings 2/3's live-axe re-check surfaced (below).

**1. Global `color-contrast` (`frontend/src/styles/tokens.css`).** Grepped
`text-text-subtle`/`text-text-muted` across `frontend/src` first (134 hits across every one of the
six surfaces plus shared `components/ui`/`components/shared`/`components/layout`) to confirm scope
before touching the shared token. Computed exact WCAG contrast ratios (relative-luminance formula,
not eyeballed) for every background each token is actually used against (`--color-surface`
white/`slate-0`, `--color-canvas` `slate-100`, `--color-surface-sunken` `slate-150` in light;
`slate-900`/`slate-950`/`slate-850` in dark) and reproduced both numbers P4-T09 cited exactly:
`--color-text-subtle` (`slate-400`, `#8e9eb4`) on white = **2.74:1** (matches the reported 2.72:1);
`--color-text-muted` (`slate-500`) on `--color-surface-sunken` (the `<Badge tone="neutral">` /
`<ProjectStatusBadge>` "In Queue" pill background) = **4.14:1** exact match to P4-T09's cited
number — confirming `text-muted` was in the failing set too, not just `text-subtle`, per the P4-T11
plan's "and its `text-muted` sibling if that's also in the failing set" instruction.

Fix: added two new dedicated primitive steps to the slate ramp (`--slate-450: 215 20% 42%` and
`--slate-550: 215 20% 56%`) rather than changing any existing primitive in place, so no other
semantic token that reuses `slate-400`/`slate-500`/`slate-600` (borders, `--color-band-p4`,
`--color-band-q`, Gantt grid colours, dark-mode primary, etc.) is affected — verified no other
semantic alias points at these two new steps. Repointed:

| Token | Theme | Before | After | Worst-case contrast before → after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--color-text-subtle` | light | `--slate-400` (`#8e9eb4`) | `--slate-450` (`#566881`) | 2.74:1 (white) → **4.84:1** (sunken, the hardest bg) |
| `--color-text-muted` | light | `--slate-500` (`#637288`) | `--slate-600` (`#465467`) | 4.14:1 (sunken) → **6.52:1** (sunken) |
| `--color-text-subtle` | dark | `--slate-500` (`#637288`) | `--slate-550` (`#788ba5`) | 3.54:1 (sunken) → **4.98:1** (sunken) |
| `--color-text-muted` | dark | `--slate-400` (`#8e9eb4`) | unchanged | already 6.31:1 minimum — passing, left alone |

Every new value clears WCAG AA's 4.5:1 (normal text) with a real margin (minimum 4.84:1, not a
borderline 4.50–4.51) against every background each token is actually composited over in the app,
computed for all three light backgrounds and all three dark backgrounds, not just white/black.
Design-hierarchy check: light theme ordering `--color-text` (slate-900, darkest/most prominent) >
`--color-text-muted` (slate-600) > `--color-text-subtle` (slate-450, lightest of the three) is
preserved; dark theme mirrors it (`--color-text` slate-100 lightest/most prominent > `--color-text-
muted` slate-400 > `--color-text-subtle` slate-550, darkest of the three) — subtle stays visibly
less prominent than muted in both themes, so this reads as a deliberate two-step darkening of the
existing ramp, not an arbitrary "just clear 4.5" patch.

**2. Registration CRITICAL `aria-required-children` (`project-list.tsx`).** Read
`virtual-matrix-grid.tsx` (Matrix) first, confirmed it never triggers this rule because every direct
child of its `role="row"` elements already carries `role="columnheader"`/`role="cell"` — Gantt's own
virtualized list (`gantt-chart.tsx`) doesn't use `role="row"`/`role="table"` ARIA at all, so it was
irrelevant here since Registration's row shape (fixed flex-column layout, closer to Matrix's grid
than to Gantt's canvas rendering) matches Matrix's pattern, not Gantt's "just don't use the role"
escape hatch. Mirrored Matrix exactly: added `role="columnheader"` to each of the 8 direct children
of the sticky header `role="row"`, and `role="cell"` to each of the 8 direct children of the
per-project data `role="row"` (name+frozen-badge, hub, category, type, status-badge-wrapper,
priority, edit-button-wrapper, and a newly-added wrapper `<div role="cell">` around the
previously-bare expand/collapse `<button>`, which is now the toggle button's sole parent rather than
the button itself carrying a `cell` role — kept the interactive `<button>`'s native semantics/
`aria-expanded`/`aria-label` intact for assistive tech rather than overriding a button's role to
`cell`). Verified live (see §6): **zero `aria-required-children` violations** on Registration
afterward, confirmed on two independent fresh-seed runs. `project-list.test.tsx` needed no
selector changes — its `getByRole('button', ...)` queries are unaffected by the new wrapping `<div
role="cell">`.

**3. Dashboard `definition-list` (`bar-chart.tsx`, used twice in `pipeline-panel.tsx` — the
`aria-label="Pipeline composition..."` instance and the `.border-t`-wrapped "Active schedule run
outcome" instance, confirmed both are the same shared `<BarChart>` component, not two separate
markup bugs).** Root cause: each `<dl>` row was `<div>` (grid wrapper) containing `<dt>` + a plain
`<div role="presentation">` (the visual bar track) + `<dd>` (the numeric value) — the middle
element's tag name (`div`, not `dt`/`dd`) violated the `dl` content model axe's `definition-list`/
`only-dlitems` check enforces. First fix attempt (mid-session, before the resume) changed the tag
from `<div role="presentation">` to `<dd role="presentation">` — **this was insufficient**: live axe
still flagged it (`"dl element has direct children that are not allowed: div > [role=presentation]"`)
because `role="presentation"` strips the element's effective ARIA role for the content-model check
regardless of its tag name, so a `<dd role="presentation">` is treated identically to the original
plain `<div>`. Corrected fix: kept the `<dd>` tag but replaced `role="presentation"` with
`aria-hidden="true"` (achieves the same original intent — hiding the meaningless decorative bar
fill from assistive tech — without touching the element's role mapping used by the content-model
check). Verified live: **zero `definition-list` violations** on Dashboard afterward, confirmed on
two independent fresh-seed runs. `bar-chart.test.tsx` needed no changes (queries by text content,
not by the bar-track element).

**4. `scrollable-region-focusable` (Capacity ×1, Dashboard ×2).** Grepped
`data-testid="virtual-table-scroll"` across `frontend/src/surfaces/capacity/` and `frontend/src/
surfaces/dashboard/` per the plan's exact instruction — found it only in one file,
`frontend/src/surfaces/dashboard/components/virtual-data-table.tsx` (shared by Dashboard's
`within-year-panel.tsx` and `project-breakdown.tsx`, i.e. the "Dashboard ×2" count), with **no**
matching literal testid anywhere under `capacity/`. Added `tabIndex={0}` to that one container,
which fixed Dashboard's two instances but **introduced a new CRITICAL regression**, caught only by
re-running live axe (not by guessing): adding a bare `tabindex` attribute to a `<div>` that is a
*direct child* of a `role="table"` element makes axe's `aria-required-children` rule reject it
("Element has children which are not allowed: div[tabindex]") — `role="table"` only permits
`row`/`rowgroup` children, and an explicit `tabindex` gives the child an effective generic-widget
role incompatible with that. Root cause: `virtual-data-table.tsx` structured `role="table"` as the
*outer* element with the scrollable `overflow-auto` div nested *inside* it as one of table's
children — the opposite of `virtual-matrix-grid.tsx`'s already-clean pattern, where the scrollable
`overflow-auto` div is the *outer* element and `role="table"` is nested inside it. Restructured
`virtual-data-table.tsx` to match Matrix's pattern exactly: the `overflow-auto`+`tabIndex={0}`+
`data-testid="virtual-table-scroll"` div is now the outermost element, with `role="table"` (header
row + virtualized body) nested inside it; the header row picked up `sticky top-0 z-10` (previously
redundant/inert since the header lived entirely outside the scrollable box) so it now behaves as a
proper sticky header sharing a scroll ancestor with the body, matching Matrix's visual behaviour.
Re-ran `virtual-data-table.test.tsx`/`within-year-panel.test.tsx` — both pass unchanged (role/name/
attribute queries only, no structural coupling).

For the real, live-axe-discovered Capacity instance (since no literal `virtual-table-scroll` testid
exists there): found via a full live axe scan on `/capacity` that the actual `serious`-impact
`scrollable-region-focusable` violation is `chamber-utilization-heatmap.tsx`'s week-by-week
horizontally-scrolling wrapper (`<div className="overflow-x-auto rounded-lg border border-border">`
— genuinely overflows given the seed data's ~47 visible weeks at 2rem/column). `hub-load-panel.tsx`/
`class-breakdown-panel.tsx`'s own `overflow-x-auto` `<Table>` wrappers do **not** trigger the rule
(their column counts fit the viewport, so no actual scrollable overflow exists in the live DOM —
axe's rule only fires on elements that actually overflow at runtime, not on every `overflow-auto`/
`overflow-x-auto` class in the source). Added `tabIndex={0}` plus `role="group"` and
`aria-label="Chamber utilization by week — scrollable"` to that one wrapper (axe's own violation
`failureSummary` said "Element should have focusable content / Element should be focusable" —
`tabIndex={0}` alone satisfies that per-rule requirement; the `role`/`aria-label` were added
defensively so a keyboard user tabbing into a newly-focusable region gets an accessible name for it,
matching this repo's existing quality bar rather than a bare rule-silencing fix). Verified live:
**zero `scrollable-region-focusable` violations** on Capacity or Dashboard afterward.

**3. Structural scrutiny — `virtual-data-table.tsx`'s `role="table"`-vs-scroll-container reorder.**
Confirmed live (script-driven, real browser, real virtualized data — Dashboard's "Filtered project
breakdown" panel, 46+ rows) that this was not just an axe-compliance reshuffle:
- `scrollHeight` (1840px) > `clientHeight` (438px) on the `data-testid="virtual-table-scroll"`
  container — it is genuinely the scrollable element, not a decorative wrapper.
- Programmatically setting `scrollTop = 400` on it actually scrolled (confirmed `scrollTop` read
  back as `400`) and the virtualizer responded — rendered row count went from 25 to 36 (overscan
  window shifting as expected), i.e. `useVirtualizer`'s `getScrollElement: () => scrollRef.current`
  still resolves correctly post-reorder since `scrollRef` is still attached to the same outer,
  `overflow-auto` div regardless of where `role="table"` sits inside it.
- The container is genuinely focusable (`tabIndex={0}` lands on the correct, actually-scrollable
  element — confirmed `document.activeElement === el` after `.focus()`) and keyboard `PageDown`
  moved `scrollTop` to 398 — the accessibility fix (finding 4) and the visual/functional scroll
  behaviour are the same element, not two different ones that happen to coincide.
- `role="table"`'s children being a `role="row"` header plus a plain, roleless height-placeholder
  `<div>` (itself containing the virtualized `role="row"` items, not direct children of `role=
  "table"`) does not trip `aria-required-children` — confirmed via the live axe scan (0 instances)
  and consistent with ARIA's "flatten through elements with no explicit/generic role when computing
  required-owned-elements" behaviour, matching `virtual-matrix-grid.tsx`'s already-clean pattern the
  remediation entry says it copied.

Dashboard's own Vitest unit test (`virtual-data-table.test.tsx`) mocks `useVirtualizer` entirely, so
it never exercised real scroll behaviour before or after this reorder — this live check was
necessary precisely because the unit test couldn't have caught a scroll regression either way.

**4. Structural scrutiny — `project-list.tsx`'s expand/collapse button now wrapped in `<div
role="cell">`.** `project-list.test.tsx` (Vitest) was re-read in full: it has **no test that queries
the expand/collapse toggle button at all** (its `getByRole('button', ...)` queries are all for the
*Edit* button) — so the remediation entry's claim "`project-list.test.tsx` needed no selector
changes" is true but does not by itself demonstrate the toggle button's semantics survived the wrap;
that suite was never testing this button either before or after. Verified independently instead,
live, in a real browser against real Registration data:
- `getByRole('button', { name: 'Expand 2026 Energy Target — Coke protocol S-800' })` (matching the
  live `aria-label`) resolves to exactly 1 element through the new `role="cell"` parent — the
  accessible name computation is unaffected by the wrapping div.
- Before click: `aria-expanded="false"`, `aria-label="Expand …"`. After click:

### [2026-09-01] P5-T02 — backend-builder

**Did:** Built the backend snapshot-on-Apply mechanism per `docs/PROJECT_AND_STACK.md` §4 ("the
backend snapshots the pre-apply state to Postgres (versioned row set) before writing the new
state, so every Apply is reversible and every historical version is queryable") and §2's "every
schedule run and every priority application is versioned; historical versions are browsable and
comparable."

**Scope decision — vertical slice, not all four entity types.** Per this task's explicit
permission to scope down: built a real, tested, end-to-end path for `PriorityScore` scenario edits
only (generalising `PUT /priorities/{project_id}`, which already existed as the "before" state to
snapshot). `Project`/`Engineer`/`Chamber` diffs ("capacity, or project data" per §4's full
sentence) are **deferred to a follow-up task**, not built or stubbed here beyond the schema having
room to grow into them without another migration (`ScenarioEntityType` enum already has all four
values; `ScenarioApplyChange` already has nullable `project_id`/`hub_id` columns generic enough for
Engineer/Chamber too). Reasoning for Priority-first: it already has a live single-row write
endpoint to generalise from, and covering all four shallowly in one pass would have meant no entity
type getting a real, DB-verified atomicity/RBAC/audit test — the task's own instructions preferred
one real vertical slice over four shallow ones.

**New models** (`backend/models/scenario.py`, new `ScenarioEntityType` enum in
`backend/models/enums.py`):
- `ScenarioApplyRun` — one row per "Apply" action: `version` (unique, same `_next_version()`
  pattern as `ScheduleRun`/`PriorityApplicationRun`), `applied_by_user_id`, `notes`, plus two
  cached fields (`entity_types_touched`, `change_count`) computed once at apply time so the P5-T03
  list view doesn't need an aggregate join. No `is_active` flag — unlike `ScheduleRun`/
  `PriorityApplicationRun`, there's nothing to "activate": every Apply's writes are already live by
  definition, and every prior version stays independently queryable via `changes`.
- `ScenarioApplyChange` — immutable per-row snapshot: `entity_type` + `entity_id` (`str(row's own
  PK)`, matching `AuditLogEntry.entity_id`'s convention), `project_id`/`hub_id` (populated for the
  built `PRIORITY_SCORE` path so `services.hub_scope.hub_scope_filter` composes directly against
  `hub_id` for row-level scoping — no new scoping shape invented), `before_state` (`None` for a
  create) / `after_state` (JSONB, `services.audit_helpers.priority_score_audit_state(...)` output —
  the same redaction-audited helper the existing `PUT /priorities/{id}` audit row already uses).
  Unique on `(scenario_apply_run_id, entity_type, entity_id)`.
- **Reversibility**: no revert *endpoint* was built (correctly out of this task's scope — P5-T03's
  job per the brief), but every `ScenarioApplyChange.before_state` is a complete-enough snapshot
  (all 13 `PriorityScore` dimensions + `hard_gates` + cached band fields) that a future revert-to-
  version-N could re-write it onto the live `PriorityScore` row directly — the model docstring says
  this explicitly so a future implementer doesn't have to re-derive it.
- **Financial-field posture**: `PriorityScore` has zero financial columns, so this task's real
  write path never touches encrypted fields at all. `models/scenario.py`'s module docstring puts a
  hard requirement on any future `PROJECT` writer: it MUST go through
  `services.audit_helpers.project_audit_state(...)` (hard-redacts `customer_name`/`tcogs_eur`/
  `selling_price_eur`/`gross_margin_pct` to the literal string `"<redacted>"`), never a raw
  `Project.__dict__` dump — flagged loudly so this isn't missed when that follow-up lands.
- **GDPR posture (OQ#8)**: no new engineer workload/busy-weeks exposure. `Engineer` isn't touched by
  this task's real write path at all; the enum value exists for future use only.

**New service** (`backend/services/scenario_apply.py`): `apply_priority_score_changes(db,
principal, notes, changes)` — validates every named `project_id` (exists + hub-scoped, via
`services.hub_scope.hub_scope_filter`) and rejects an empty diff / duplicate `project_id`s **before
writing or flushing anything**, then snapshots + writes each item, `flush()`-only (never commits) so
the caller (the router) controls the single transaction boundary. Two exception types
(`ScenarioApplyValidationError` base, `ScenarioApplyNotFoundError` subclass) let the router map to
400 vs. 404 without this module importing FastAPI — mirrors `services/schedule_persistence.py`'s
"raises `ValueError`, the router translates it" convention.

**New endpoints** (`backend/api/routers/scenarios.py`, wired into `api/main.py`):
- `POST /scenarios/apply` — `MATRIX`/`WRITE` (Portfolio Manager, Admin only — Hub Planner is
  READ-only on Matrix, same restriction as the `PUT /priorities/{id}` endpoint this generalises).
  Accepts `{notes, priority_scores: [...]}`; snapshots pre-apply state, writes new
  `PriorityScore` values, writes one `AuditLogEntry` (`action="scenario_apply.apply"`,
  `entity_type="ScenarioApplyRun"`, `hub_id=None` since a batch may span hubs — same "one audit row
  per bulk op" precedent as `schedule_runs.py`'s `trigger_greedy_recalc`/`dispatch_cp_sat_run`, not
  one audit row per touched `PriorityScore`), commits once, returns the new version + suggested
  bands. 400 on empty/duplicate diff, 404 on any nonexistent/out-of-scope `project_id` (collapsed
  into one status, matching this codebase's existing "don't leak which out-of-scope rows exist"
  posture — see `_resolve_projects_in_scope`'s docstring).
- `GET /scenarios/versions` / `GET /scenarios/versions/{version}` — `MATRIX`/`READ` (Portfolio
  Manager, Hub Planner, Executive Viewer, Admin). Hub-scoped via an `EXISTS(...)` correlated
  subquery composed from `hub_scope_filter(principal, ScenarioApplyChange.hub_id)` — reused the
  existing helper's "predicate or `None`-if-unrestricted" shape directly rather than inventing a
  4th scoping shape in `services/hub_scope.py` (the inner WHERE of an EXISTS is the same predicate
  shape as a plain filter). The detail endpoint 404s (not 200-with-empty-`changes`) when a
  hub-restricted caller's scope excludes every change in that version, so as not to leak that the
  version exists at all.

**Alembic migration**: `backend/alembic/versions/7b540c00cea8_scenario_apply_versioning.py`
(`down_revision='ba3881d85b55'`) — adds `scenario_apply_runs`/`scenario_apply_changes` +
`scenario_entity_type` enum. Hand-edited from the raw `--autogenerate` output to drop two spurious
`op.drop_index`/`op.create_index` pairs for `ux_schedule_runs_one_active`/
`ux_priority_application_runs_one_active` (known false positives — those are hand-written partial
indexes with no ORM-level representation, so autogenerate proposes "removing" them on every future
diff regardless of what actually changed; same phenomenon `419f196fd00b`'s own migration already
documents). Added an explicit `DROP TYPE IF EXISTS scenario_entity_type` to `downgrade()` after
initially assuming (wrongly — corrected after an empirical failure, see below) that `op.drop_table`
auto-drops an inline `sa.Enum`'s Postgres type; `419f196fd00b`'s own downgrade already does this
explicitly for its 12 enum types and I initially missed why, then hit the exact
`DuplicateObjectError` that comment predicts, on a second `upgrade head` after a `downgrade base`
that hadn't dropped the type — fixed, then re-verified clean.

**Verification performed:**
- Migration cycle (own throwaway `postgres:17` Docker container, not the pytest testcontainers
  fixture): `upgrade head` → `downgrade base` → `upgrade head` → `downgrade base`, twice through,
  all clean; `alembic revision --autogenerate` at head produces zero diff beyond the two documented
  pre-existing partial-index false positives (confirmed no scenario-table drift proposed).
  `tests/test_migrations.py`'s `EXPECTED_TABLE_COUNT` (19→21) and `EXPECTED_ENUM_TYPES` (added
  `scenario_entity_type`) updated to match; that test itself re-run and passing.
- New `tests/test_scenario_apply_api.py` — **18 passed**: apply creates a snapshot for a new
  `PriorityScore` (before_state=None) and for an update (before_state populated with the old
  values); audit-log row written with the right action/entity/summary; batching multiple projects
  in one version; empty-diff and duplicate-project-id both 400; an out-of-scope project 404s;
  **atomicity**: (a) HTTP-layer — a batch with one valid + one nonexistent project 404s and writes
  NOTHING, not even the valid item (`test_apply_all_or_nothing_on_invalid_item`); (b) service-layer
  — a monkeypatched failure on the *second* item of a two-item batch, after the first item's
  `PriorityScore`/`ScenarioApplyRun` are already flushed (real partial work happened), confirms an
  `await db_session.rollback()` (exactly what `api.db.get_db`'s `async with session_factory() as
  session:` does automatically on an unhandled exception in production) discards BOTH items, not
  just the one that failed (`test_apply_service_atomic_on_mid_batch_failure`); RBAC negative tests
  (401 unauthenticated, 403 Hub Planner on WRITE, 403 Engineer, 403 Engineer on the list endpoint);

  hub's version 404s on direct fetch); versions list/detail round-trip.
- Full backend suite: `python -m pytest -q` → **357 passed** (was 339 pre-task; +18 new), **87.57%
  coverage** (was 86.58%) — **≥70% gate: CONFIRMED PASSING.**
- Scheduling suite: `python -m pytest -c pytest-scheduling.ini -q` → **80 passed, 93.58% coverage**

- `ruff check .` → **all checks passed** (0 errors, matching baseline) after one auto-`--fix` (two

- `mypy .` (full, unscoped) → **608 errors in 47 files** (was 561 at P3-T09's last documented full
  run). Confirmed the delta is NOT a regression in untouched code: filtering out every error whose

### [2026-09-01] P5-T01 — frontend-builder

**Did:** Built scenario-edit state for priority scores per `docs/PROJECT_AND_STACK.md` §4's
"A 'scenario' … is held in frontend Zustand state and, on 'Apply', POSTed as a diff against the
last committed version" — scoped explicitly to priority-score edits only, matching P5-T02's backend
contract (`POST /scenarios/apply` only accepts `priority_scores` diffs today; `Project`/`Engineer`/
`Chamber` scenario edits have no backend path yet, per that task's flagged follow-up). Read
`backend/schemas/scenario.py` and `backend/api/routers/scenarios.py` directly before building the
frontend types — confirmed `ScenarioPriorityScoreChange` is a FULL-ROW replacement per project (all
13 dims `ge=1 le=5`, none optional/nullable, `extra="forbid"`), not a sparse per-field diff, so the
Apply payload is "one full-row entry per genuinely-changed project," not a field-level patch.

**New Zustand store** (`frontend/src/stores/scenario.ts`, the location `stores/ui.ts`'s own
docstring already earmarked for this) — `useScenarioStore`:
- `active` (scenario-mode toggle), `notes` (free text for `ScenarioApplyRequest.notes`, NOT part of
  undo/redo), `pending` (`Record<projectId, ScenarioPendingEdit>`), `past`/`future` (simple
  snapshot-of-the-whole-`pending`-map stacks — "a simple past/future stack … is enough" per the
  task brief).
- `ScenarioPendingEdit` = `{ projectId, projectName, hub, baseline, hasScore, next }`. `baseline` is
  captured from the live `PriorityScoreUpdateRequest` values ONLY on a project's first stage in the
  current scenario — re-staging the same project before Apply updates `next` only, never rebases
  `baseline` (verified by a dedicated test: passing a different/stale `liveValues` on a second
  `stageEdit` call for the same project does not change what `baseline` holds). This is what makes
  "diffed against last committed version" correct even across multiple edits of the same project in
  one scenario.
- **Correctness finding, not in the original brief — flagged and fixed**: an unscored project
  (`has_score=false`) has no real committed value to diff against; the edit dialog pre-fills such a
  project's form with a neutral 3/5 default (existing `dimensionDefaultsFromRow` convention). Naively
  diffing `next` against that same 3/5 default as "baseline" would make a first-time score submitted
  with all-default values look like a no-op and get silently dropped from the Apply payload — which
  would be wrong: creating a score for a previously-unscored project is always a genuine change,
  regardless of what the values happen to be. Added `hasScore` to `ScenarioPendingEdit` (captured
  once, same as `baseline`) and made `isNoOpEdit` return `false` unconditionally when `!hasScore`.
  Covered by tests in both `stores/scenario.test.ts` and `scenario-panel.test.tsx` ("New score"
  badge).
- **Undo/redo**: standard array-stack semantics — `stageEdit`/`removeEdit` push the prior `pending`
  map onto `past` and clear `future`; `undo`/`redo` move the whole map between `past`/`pending`/
  `future`. Staging a new edit after an undo correctly prunes the redo branch (tested explicitly:
  stage A, stage B, undo, stage C — redo is then inert, matching standard editor undo/redo
  semantics, not a linear history that would let C rejoin B's branch).
- `computeScenarioDiff(pending)` / `effectivePendingEdits(pending)` / `isNoOpEdit(edit)` — pure,
  exported functions. `computeScenarioDiff` is what gets POSTed: filters out no-op edits, maps the
  rest to `{ project_id, ...next }` — exactly `ScenarioPriorityScoreChange[]`.
- No `persist` middleware — an in-progress scenario is intentionally ephemeral; a refresh abandoning
  unsaved staged edits is treated as expected, conservative behaviour, not a gap to paper over.

**Types** (`frontend/src/surfaces/matrix/api/types.ts`, additive, following this repo's established
hand-authored-mirror convention): `ScenarioPriorityScoreChange`, `ScenarioApplyRequest`,
`ScenarioApplyRunSummary`, `ScenarioApplyResponse` — hand-mirrored from `backend/schemas/
scenario.py`'s exact field set (`ScenarioApplyRequest.notes?`/`priority_scores`, nothing else,
matching `extra="forbid"`).

**API + hook** (`frontend/src/surfaces/matrix/api/matrix-api.ts` / `hooks/use-matrix.ts`):
`applyScenario(body)` → `POST /scenarios/apply`; `useApplyScenario()` mutation, `onSuccess`
invalidates `['priority-matrix']` only — deliberately does NOT invalidate `['schedule-runs', …]`/
`['capacity', …]`/`['gantt', …]`/`['dashboard', …]`, for the identical reason `useUpdatePriorityScore`
already doesn't: a scenario Apply only ever writes `PriorityScore` rows today (P5-T02's contract
limit), never triggers a schedule run, and Invariant I9 forbids inferring a schedule-derived number
from anything other than an actual solver run — confirmed this reasoning against the existing
`useUpdatePriorityScore` precedent and its own test (`use-matrix.test.tsx`) before applying it to the
new hook, rather than assuming it.

**UI** (`frontend/src/surfaces/matrix/components/scenario-panel.tsx`, new) — additive to the existing
Matrix surface, does not remove or alter the immediate-write flow's own code path:
- `ScenarioModeToggle` — a checkbox in the Matrix "View" filters card. Fixed a real accessible-name
  bug caught before shipping: the group heading ("Edit mode") and the checkbox's own label
  ("Scenario mode") were both initially wired to the SAME `htmlFor`/`id`, which would have made the
  checkbox's accessible name the concatenation of both labels' text ("Edit mode Scenario mode")
  instead of just "Scenario mode" — split into two distinct ids (`groupId` via `aria-labelledby` on
  a `role="group"` wrapper, `checkboxId` via the checkbox's own `<label htmlFor>`) before any test
  was written against the accessible name, so this was caught by construction, not by a failing test.
- `ScenarioPendingPanel` — lists every staged edit with a raw field-for-field diff (dimension label,
  before → after, read directly from `baseline`/`next` — never a recomputed score/band/currency
  figure; Invariant I9 applies to display logic too, not just to what's sent over the wire), a
  "New score" badge for previously-unscored projects, a "No change" badge for a staged-then-reverted
  no-op, a per-row Remove button, Undo/Redo, a free-text notes field, and Apply/Discard. Apply is
  disabled when there are zero genuinely-changed staged edits (a scenario of only no-ops has nothing
  to send) or when `writeForbidden` (mirrors the immediate-edit flow's own RBAC-discovered-after-a-
  403 posture, not proactive role introspection — same limitation the immediate flow already has).
- `score-edit-dialog.tsx` gained an additive `mode?: 'immediate' | 'scenario'` prop (`@default
  'immediate'`) that only changes copy/button text ("Save score" vs. "Stage change", etc.) — the
  form fields, validation, and `onSubmit` contract are byte-identical between modes; the existing
  `score-edit-dialog.test.tsx` file was NOT modified and still passes unchanged, confirming the
  default path is untouched.
- `matrix-table.tsx` gained an additive optional `scenarioStagedProjectIds` prop — a small "Staged"
  badge next to the Edit button for rows with a genuinely-changed pending edit; `undefined` (the
  default when the prop is omitted) renders nothing, so `matrix-table.test.tsx` needed no changes
  and still passes unchanged.
- `MatrixPage.tsx` wires it together: `handleSubmit` branches on `scenarioActive` — scenario mode
  calls `stageEdit(...)` (passing the ORIGINAL live row's values as `liveValues`/`liveHasScore`,
  captured via a new `liveRequestValuesFromRow` helper added to `score-edit-schema.ts`) and returns
  without any network call; immediate mode is the exact pre-existing `updateScore.mutateAsync` path,
  untouched. Re-opening the edit dialog for a project that already has a staged edit pre-fills from
  the staged `next` values (via a `dialogRow` memo merging `editRow` with any staged edit) rather
  than the stale live ones, so continuing an edit feels natural — `editRow` itself always stays the
  true original live row, which is what the baseline capture actually needs.

### [2026-09-02] P5-T04 — CSV/XLSX export for every surface, via MinIO for large exports — backend-builder

**Did:** Built the cross-cutting "Downloads" feature (`docs/PROJECT_AND_STACK.md` §2) for all six
surfaces — two paths sharing one implementation, per this task's own guidance to look at what
exists rather than inventing a new mechanism:

1. **Synchronous (default)**: `GET /exports/{surface}?format=csv|xlsx` streams the file inline,
   no MinIO/Celery involved. Appropriate at this app's real scale (~236 projects portfolio-wide,
   per CLAUDE.md — even an unfiltered Gantt flattened export is a few thousand rows, sub-second).
2. **Async ("large export, via MinIO")**: `?async_export=true` instead creates a durable
   `models.export.ExportJob` row and dispatches `workers.export_tasks.generate_export` onto a
   **new, separate** general-purpose `worker` Celery process (`workers/worker_app.py`) — distinct
   from `workers/celery_app.py` ("solver-worker"), per `docs/PROJECT_AND_STACK.md` §6's own
   deployment topology ("worker (Celery — general background jobs: exports, notifications)" vs.
   "solver-worker (CP-SAT and greedy scheduler runs, isolated for resource limits)"). The task
   writes the finished file to MinIO (new `core/minio_config.py`, env-driven `RPD_MINIO_*` settings,
   mirroring `core/config.py`/`core/celery_config.py`'s established lazy-singleton pattern) and the
   caller polls `GET /exports/jobs/{id}` for status, then `GET /exports/jobs/{id}/download` (a
   server-side proxy through FastAPI, not a presigned MinIO URL — the on-prem topology doesn't
   guarantee MinIO is browser-reachable) once `completed`. Chose the simpler poll-based design over
   an SSE progress stream, as this task's brief explicitly allowed — real export generation at this
   app's scale is expected to complete in low single-digit seconds, nowhere near CP-SAT's
   up-to-a-minute-plus solves that motivated `workers/progress.py`'s SSE relay.

**Single shared implementation, not two parallel ones** (`services/export_builder.py`): both paths
call the exact same per-surface builder functions, which in turn call THAT surface's own existing
read-endpoint function directly, in-process (`api.routers.dashboard.analytics_projects`,
`api.routers.capacity.hub_load_vs_capacity`, `api.routers.priorities.list_priority_matrix`,
`api.routers.gantt.get_gantt`, `api.routers.projects.list_projects`,
`api.routers.engineers.list_engineers`, `api.routers.chambers.list_chambers`) — passing through
the real `db`/`current_user` (`core.principal.Principal`). This is the mechanism that satisfies "an
export is a read operation and must never leak data a user's role/hub scope wouldn't let them see
via the API": every one of those functions already applies `services.hub_scope` filtering and (for
Gantt) the GDPR engineer-name-withholding gate (`docs/OPEN_QUESTIONS.md` #8) internally — an export
can never expose a row or field its caller's role/hub scope wouldn't already show via the ordinary
endpoint, because it *is* that endpoint's own output, reshaped. RBAC is one `require_permission`
dependency per surface, reusing `core.rbac.Surface`/`Action` exactly as that surface's own router
does (`DASHBOARD/READ`, `CAPACITY/READ`, `MATRIX/READ`, `GANTT/READ`, `PROJECT_REGISTRATION/READ`,
`CAPACITY_PLANNING/READ`) — never a separately-derived "can this role export" concept.

**Financial fields exported like any other authorized field, never logged**: Matrix and Project
Registration exports include the four CLAUDE.md-named encrypted fields (`tcogs_eur`,
`selling_price_eur`, `gross_margin_pct`, `customer_name`) exactly because the reused read endpoints
already serve them to an authorized caller — verified end-to-end in both `tests/test_export_api.py`
(sync path) and `tests/test_export_worker_task.py` (async path, real MinIO round-trip). No log line
anywhere in `workers/export_tasks.py` contains a row's actual values — only `export_job_id`,
`surface`, `format`, and integer row *counts* (confirmed by reading the module's own logger calls).

**Async job authorization is owner-scoped, not surface-RBAC-scoped**: `GET /exports/jobs/{id}` and
`.../download` check `ExportJob.requested_by_user_id == current_user.user_id` OR Admin, returning
404 (never 403) for anyone else — matching this codebase's established "hub-scope mismatch reads as
not-found" convention rather than confirming a job's existence to an unauthorized caller. The Celery
task reconstructs the dispatching caller's exact `Principal` (roles/hub_ids/user_id, serialized to a
plain JSON dict at dispatch time, in `api/routers/exports.py::_principal_to_task_payload` /
`workers/export_tasks.py::_principal_from_payload`) so the async path's RBAC/hub-scope enforcement
is byte-identical to what the original HTTP request had — never a re-authentication, never a wider
grant.

**New models/migration**: `models.export.ExportJob` (mirrors `ScheduleRun`'s "one row per
background job" shape) + `models.enums.ExportSurface`/`ExportFormat`/`ExportJobStatus` (duplicated,
not imported, from `core.rbac.Surface` — `models/` must never depend on `core/`, confirmed by
grepping existing imports first) + Alembic migration `d113ff5e8e17_export_jobs.py` (hand-edited to
drop the same two spurious partial-unique-index autogenerate false-positives `7b540c00cea8`'s own
migration already documents — `ux_schedule_runs_one_active`/`ux_priority_application_runs_one_active`
have no ORM-level representation and always show as "diff" regardless of what actually changed).
`ExportJob.filters` stores only plain query-filter-parameter echoes (hub_id/category/currency/etc.
as strings), never row data — verified by reading `models/export.py`'s own docstring reasoning
against `models.scenario.ScenarioApplyChange`'s "never a raw dump" precedent. `tests/
test_migrations.py`'s `EXPECTED_TABLE_COUNT` (21→22) / `EXPECTED_ENUM_TYPES` (+3) updated to match;
full up→down→up→down cycle re-verified against a dedicated throwaway Postgres container.

**Export-only, no import path built** (P5-T05 scope-lock, already recorded DONE in
`docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`) — nothing in this task accepts an uploaded CSV/XLSX. Not revisited.

**Deliberately out of scope / left for follow-up:**

**Did:** Closed the gap flagged in P5-T04's entry: `frontend/src/surfaces/matrix/api/types.ts`'s

`RPD_REDIS_URL` set the same way `tests/conftest.py` does) to inspect the actual `components/schemas`
shapes before wiring anything up.

Six of the seven map to a real, directly-checkable backend OpenAPI component and were added to
`CONTRACT_TABLE` in `mode="exact"`, field-for-field: `ScenarioPriorityScoreChange`,
`ScenarioApplyRequest`, `ScenarioApplyResponse`, `ScenarioApplyRunSummary`, `ScenarioApplyRunDetail`,
`ScenarioApplyChangeDetail`. Verified by hand against the generated schema that field sets and
required-ness match exactly (including the deliberate, already-established asymmetry the test itself
documents: TS marking a field required that the backend leaves optional-with-default, e.g.

absent. Reason: on the backend it exists only as the Pydantic base class of

emits it as its own component (it gets flattened into `ScenarioApplyChangeDetail`'s properties
instead). The frontend interface has the exact same role — grepped `frontend/src` and confirmed
`ScenarioApplyChangeSummary` is only ever `extends`ed by the frontend `ScenarioApplyChangeDetail`,

OpenAPI-based `_backend_fields()` helper can address by name on its own) or (b) inventing a synthetic
backend schema, added it to `CONTRACT_TABLE` in `mode="subset"` against `ScenarioApplyChangeDetail`
— the actual wire schema that contains it — exactly mirroring the pre-existing
`GanttActiveRun -> ScheduleRunSummary "subset"` precedent already in this table for the identical
"reduced view of a larger real schema" shape. This gives a genuine field-for-field check (all 5
summary fields confirmed present in the real `ScenarioApplyChangeDetail` schema) rather than a
silenced/loosened one. No mismatch was found anywhere in this pass — all seven interfaces were
accurate mirrors of the real backend shapes; nothing needed correcting on either side.

right after `services/notifications.py` and `services/schedule_persistence.py`'s wiring were written
but *before* `schemas/notification.py`/`api/routers/notifications.py` were finished and *before*

touched before the cutoff (`models/notification.py`, `services/notifications.py`,
`services/schedule_persistence.py`, `models/__init__.py`, `models/enums.py`, the migration) — all
syntactically intact, no half-written code found. The one real gap: `api/main.py` had NOT yet been
edited to `include_router` the new notifications router (confirmed by grepping for "notification" in
that file — zero hits). Fixed by finishing `schemas/notification.py`/`api/routers/notifications.py`
(already drafted in-session before the cutoff per the transcript, re-verified by reading them back)
and wiring `api/main.py`. Verified the fix by generating `app.openapi()` in-process and confirming
`/notifications`, `/notifications/{id}/read`, `/notifications/read-all` are real, registered paths —
not just importable modules.

**Did:** Built in-app notifications per `docs/PROJECT_AND_STACK.md` §2's "in-app notification of
schedule changes affecting a user's hub or assigned projects (delay introduced, project left out,
conflict raised)." Read `services/schedule_persistence.py`, `workers/schedule_tasks.py`,
`api/routers/schedule_runs.py`, `core/rbac.py`, `core/principal.py`, `services/hub_scope.py`,
`api/routers/gantt.py` (the engineer-self-scoping precedent) directly before designing anything, per
the task brief's instruction not to invent parallel infrastructure.

**Diff-trigger mechanism (the key design decision)**: no new event bus, no second detection path.
`services/notifications.py::generate_schedule_change_notifications` is called from EXACTLY ONE place
— `services/schedule_persistence.py::persist_schedule_output`, immediately after a newly-activated
`ScheduleRun`'s (`activate=True`) outcome/step rows are written, diffing the new run's in-memory
`ScheduleOutput.project_outcomes` (already computed by the caller — never re-read from the DB) against
whatever `ScheduleRun` was `is_active` immediately before this call (captured via a `SELECT` *before*
the existing deactivate `UPDATE` runs, so the baseline id is never lost). **Deliberately gated on
`activate=True` only** — a completed-but-not-activated CP-SAT run (`workers/schedule_tasks.py`'s
current "CP-SAT never auto-activates" decision, P3-T06) never generates notifications, since
notifications describe changes to the schedule a user's UI actually reflects, never a hypothetical,
unreviewed result nobody has applied. Verified this gating with a direct test
(`test_persist_schedule_output_generates_notifications_only_when_activated`): a third
`persist_schedule_output(activate=False, sync_live_workflow_steps=False)` call with an even-worse
outcome produces zero `Notification` rows, confirming the gate is real, not just documented. A
project absent from the previous run's outcomes (new to the portfolio) is skipped entirely for all
three reasons — there is no known prior baseline to regress from, so nothing about a brand-new
project's first schedule outcome is honestly a "change." `LEFT_OUT` suppresses a redundant
`DELAY_INTRODUCED` for the same project in the same pass (a project that just became left-out gets
only the more severe reason). `CONFLICT_RAISED`'s previous-run signal is derived via
`bool_or(eng_conflict), bool_or(chamber_overlap)` over `ScheduleRunProjectStep` (grouped by
`project_id`) since `ScheduleRunProjectOutcome` itself has no conflict columns — only the per-step
snapshot table does.

**Recipient scoping (the other key design decision)**: reused `core.rbac.role_allows` and the exact
`(DASHBOARD, CAPACITY, GANTT)` surface triple `api/routers/schedule_runs.py`'s own `_read_any`
already uses for "who can see schedule-run-derived data" (MATRIX deliberately excluded — it concerns
priority-score edits, not delay/left-out/conflict outcomes), rather than inventing a new
audience/subscription system. A user is a recipient of a given event iff their role(s) grant READ on
at least one of those three surfaces AND (hub_scope_all=True, OR explicitly `UserHubScope`'d to the
event's project's hub, OR holds the Engineer role and is the linked `User` for that project's
`Project.leader_engineer_id` — the GDPR-conscious "own assigned projects only" narrowing named in the
brief, matching `services.hub_scope.is_engineer_self_scoped`'s existing Gantt precedent; an Engineer
never sees a notification about a project they don't lead, even one in a hub they're otherwise linked
to). Auditor is never a recipient (grants nothing on those three surfaces) — verified explicitly
(`test_auditor_is_never_a_recipient`). Inactive users are excluded (`User.is_active` filter). A user
matching more than one path (e.g. Engineer *and* Hub-Planner-scoped to the same hub) still gets
exactly ONE row — recipients are deduplicated by user id before any row is written, verified
(`test_dedup_when_user_matches_hub_scope_and_engineer_path`).

**Model — fanout-per-recipient, not event+join-table**: `models/notification.py`'s new `Notification`
table is one row PER (event, recipient) pair, with `read_at` directly on the row (matching the task
brief's literal suggested shape most closely) rather than a single event row plus a separate
`NotificationRead(notification_id, user_id, read_at)` join table. Trade-off recorded explicitly in the
model's own docstring: audience membership is snapshotted at generation time — a user added to a hub
(or promoted) AFTER a notification was generated will not retroactively see it, even though a live
query would now include them. Judged acceptable (an in-app feed is forward-looking, not a retroactive
audit trail — `AuditLogEntry` already exists for that, unaffected). Columns:
`recipient_user_id`/`reason` (`NotificationReason` enum, `models/enums.py`)/`project_id`(required —
all three reasons are inherently per-project)/`hub_id` (denormalised, same rationale as
`ScenarioApplyChange.hub_id`)/`message` (free text)/`schedule_run_id`/`previous_schedule_run_id`
(both FK `schedule_runs.id`)/`read_at`. No explicit composite index added (`(recipient_user_id,
read_at)` etc.) — matches this codebase's existing convention of not adding performance indexes
beyond what migrations already have (e.g. `audit_log_entries.actor_user_id` has none either); flagged
as a real, deferred optimization if notification volume grows.

**Financial fields**: `message` is composed only from `Project.name`/`Hub.name`/plain integer week
numbers (`services/notifications.py::_reason_message`) — never `tcogs_eur`/`selling_price_eur`/
`gross_margin_pct`/`customer_name`, verified by an explicit `"$" not in message` assertion in tests.

**API** (`api/routers/notifications.py`, all under `Depends(get_current_principal)`, deliberately
**no** `require_permission`/`require_roles` — checked `core/rbac.py` first, per the brief, and found
no existing per-user-not-per-surface precedent; every `Surface` maps to one of the six client-facing
surfaces plus Audit Log/User-Role-Admin, none of them "a user's own inbox"): `GET /notifications`
(`unread_only` filter, `limit`/`offset` pagination validated `[1,200]`/`>=0` per this codebase's
established convention, unread-first-then-newest ordering, `unread_count` always reflects the
caller's TOTAL unread count regardless of the `unread_only` filter so a UI badge doesn't need a
second request), `POST /notifications/{id}/read` (idempotent, 404 — never 403 — for a nonexistent or
someone-else's notification, matching this codebase's established not-found-over-403 convention),
`POST /notifications/read-all` (bulk, SELECT-then-UPDATE-by-id-list rather than relying on the
`UPDATE` result's `.rowcount`, since `AsyncSession.execute(...)`'s declared return type doesn't expose
that attribute under strict mypy). Both mutations write an `AuditLogEntry`
(`notification.read`/`notification.read_all`) per CLAUDE.md's "every mutation" rule, even though this
is a trivial personal-UX state change, not a business-data mutation — erred toward the rule's letter.
Row-level scoping is `recipient_user_id == current_user.user_id` on every query (not
`services.hub_scope.hub_scope_filter` — a `Notification` row already encodes its recipient at
generation time; there's nothing left to hub-scope at read time).

**No SSE, no email/Slack/push** — a plain pollable `GET /notifications` list satisfies "in-app" per
the task brief's own guidance; real solver-progress SSE (`workers/progress.py`) exists for a
materially different problem (a single long-running job's live status), not a fit for a personal,
potentially-multi-event inbox.
