### [2026-09-07] P7-T06 — backend-builder: off-host mirror of the nightly MinIO backup bucket

**Did:** Followed the Memory Protocol: read `docs/DOMAIN_RULES.md` in full, the tail of
`docs/MEMORY.md` (my own two most recent P7-T03-part-1 entries and frontend-builder's P7-T03-part-2
entry, both immediately above this one), and `docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`'s P7-T06 entry. Also read
`backend/workers/backup_tasks.py`, `backend/workers/restore_backup.py`,
`backend/core/minio_config.py`, `backend/workers/worker_app.py`, `backend/docker-entrypoint.sh`,
`backend/Dockerfile`, `docker-compose.yml`, `.env.example`, `secrets/README.md`, and the existing
`backend/tests/test_workers_backup_tasks.py` / `test_workers_restore_backup.py` before writing
anything, so the new task matches this repo's established Celery/MinIO/secrets patterns exactly
rather than inventing a new convention. No `backend/scheduling/` file read or touched.

**Built:**
- `backend/core/backup_mirror_config.py` (new) — `BackupMirrorSettings` (`RPD_BACKUP_MIRROR_`
  prefix: `endpoint`/`bucket`/`access_key`/`secret_key`/`secure`, all optional, all blank by
  default), an `is_configured` property, and `get_backup_mirror_client()` returning `None` (not
  raising) when unconfigured — a deliberate, documented asymmetry from `MinioSettings`'s own
  fail-loudly-if-unset convention, since the off-host destination is Frigoglass's own infrastructure
  decision and has not been made yet (P7-T06's own acceptance criteria: "implement against a
  configurable target, do not hardcode one").
- `backend/workers/backup_mirror_tasks.py` (new) — `mirror_backups_offhost` Celery task. No-ops
  (`status: "skipped"`) when the destination isn't configured; otherwise lists every object in the
  local `rpd-backups` bucket, skips any that already exist at the destination with a matching size
  (`mc mirror`'s own default comparison), and copies the rest via a source `fget_object` ->
  destination `fput_object` round-trip through a temp file — the exact same download/upload shape
  `workers/restore_backup.py` already uses, so no new I/O pattern was introduced. Implemented with
  the `minio` Python SDK (already a dependency, `pyproject.toml`) rather than shelling out to an `mc`
  binary, because the backend image (`backend/Dockerfile`) does not ship one and adding a second
  binary just for this one task seemed like an unjustified image-size/attack-surface increase versus
  reusing the SDK this codebase already depends on for identical object-copy operations elsewhere —
  functionally equivalent to `mc mirror <source> <dest>` (one-way, skip-existing, never deletes),
  documented as such in the module's own docstring so a future reader doesn't wonder why the task
  brief's suggested tool isn't literally invoked. Best-effort per-object: one failed object does not
  abort the rest of the pass, but the task as a whole raises (Celery FAILURE) if any object failed,
  so a partial mirror is never silently reported as `"completed"`.
- `backend/workers/worker_app.py` — added `workers.backup_mirror_tasks` to the existing `worker`
  Celery app's `include=[...]` list (same app/queue as `workers.backup_tasks`, for the identical
  resource-isolation reasoning already documented there — this is not CP-SAT-scale work and does not
  belong on `solver-worker`), and a new `beat_schedule` entry (`nightly-backup-offhost-mirror`,
  03:00 UTC — one hour after the existing 02:00 UTC nightly `pg_dump`). Deliberately NOT chained
  directly off the pg_dump task's own success (no `.apply_async(link=...)`) so a pg_dump failure on
  one night never blocks mirroring of previous, still-unmirrored backups — the mirror task always
  scans the whole bucket, so a late-finishing dump is simply picked up the following night instead of
  being missed.
- `backend/docker-entrypoint.sh` — added two more `resolve_secret` calls
  (`RPD_BACKUP_MIRROR_ACCESS_KEY`/`RPD_BACKUP_MIRROR_SECRET_KEY`), confirmed harmless no-ops today
  (the resolver's own logic returns immediately if the corresponding `_FILE` var isn't set — verified
  by reading the function, not assumed) since neither is wired into `docker-compose.yml` yet — exact
  same "add now, wire later" pattern already established for the OIDC confidential-client-secret
  future slot in the same file.
- `docker-compose.yml` — added three plain **config** env vars to the `x-backend-image` anchor
  (`RPD_BACKUP_MIRROR_ENDPOINT`/`BUCKET`/`SECURE`, all with safe blank/`true` defaults via `${VAR:-}`
  interpolation), plus a commented-out future-slot block for the two **secret** `_FILE` env vars,
  mirroring the existing commented-out OIDC client-secret slot immediately above it in the same file.
  **Judgment call, documented inline in both `docker-compose.yml` and `secrets/README.md`:**
  deliberately did NOT add `backup_mirror_access_key`/`backup_mirror_secret_key` to the top-level
  `secrets:` map or the anchor's `secrets:` list yet, because Compose refuses to bring up ANY service
  in the stack if a listed secret's `file:` doesn't exist on the deploying host — doing so today would
  force every current Frigoglass deployment (none of which has chosen an off-host destination yet) to
  create two placeholder credential files just to run `docker compose up` at all. Verified this
  reasoning empirically, not just by reading the Compose docs: `docker compose config --quiet`
  (v5.3.0, this environment) resolves the edited file cleanly with the four pre-existing secret files
  only — no new secret file was required to bring the stack config up, confirming the commented-out
  approach doesn't add a new precondition. Independently confirmed via `docker compose config` that
  `RPD_BACKUP_MIRROR_ENDPOINT`/`BUCKET` render as empty strings and `RPD_BACKUP_MIRROR_SECURE`
  renders as `"true"` when unset, i.e. the shipped default is genuinely inert.
- `.env.example` — added `RPD_BACKUP_MIRROR_ENDPOINT`/`RPD_BACKUP_MIRROR_BUCKET` (blank placeholders)
  and `RPD_BACKUP_MIRROR_SECURE=true`, with a comment pointing at `secrets/README.md` for the
  credential half and at `docs/HANDOVER/BACKUP_RESTORE.md` §4 for the full explanation. No real
  hostname, bucket name, or credential anywhere.
- `secrets/README.md` — new "Future slot: off-host backup mirror" section (same structure/tone as
  the existing OIDC client-secret future-slot section), naming
  `secrets/backup_mirror_access_key.txt` / `secrets/backup_mirror_secret_key.txt` as the two files an
  operator creates once Frigoglass picks a destination, and the exact `docker-compose.yml` lines to
  uncomment at that point.
- `docs/HANDOVER/BACKUP_RESTORE.md` §4 — fully rewritten (was previously my own P7-T03 "recommended,
  not automated, `mc mirror` as a suggestion" text) into: 4.1 what the mirror mechanism actually does
  and its scheduling relationship to the nightly dump, 4.2 how to configure a real destination
  (config vs. secret split, cross-referenced to `secrets/README.md`), 4.3 how to verify it's running
  (log lines to check, and an explicit "a `skipped` status is not a problem if unconfigured" callout
  so an operator doesn't chase a non-issue), and 4.4 how this fits into the restore procedure —
  concretely: if the primary host is a total loss, point `RPD_MINIO_*` at the mirror target's own
  connection details (simplest) or copy the needed object into a fresh `minio` service first, then
  proceed with §3's existing restore procedure unchanged; also re-emphasized that the
  field-encryption key (§5) is a wholly separate dependency the mirror does not cover. Also updated

  Left `rpd-exports` explicitly out of scope (regenerable on demand, no total-loss risk), consistent
  with the original §4's own reasoning.

  - `api/types.ts` — `AuditLogEntry`/`AuditLogEntryList`/`AuditLogFilterParams`, field names copied
    verbatim from `backend/schemas/audit.py`.
  - `api/audit-log-api.ts` (+ `.test.ts`) — thin `apiGet` wrapper, no transformation.
  - `hooks/use-audit-log.ts` — TanStack Query hook, `retryUnlessAuth` (same convention as every other
    surface's hook), `placeholderData: (prev) => prev` so a filter/pagination change doesn't flash
    to empty.
  - `hooks/use-debounced-value.ts` (new, small, surface-scoped) — debounces the four free-text
    filters (entity type/ID, actor, action) before they hit the query key. Not promoted to a shared
    hook: this is the first free-text filter in the app (every other surface's filters are
    `<Select>`s that only change on a discrete pick), so there's no second caller yet to justify a
    shared abstraction.
  - `components/access-notice.tsx` — same `AccessNotice` pattern as every other surface, wording
    scoped to "Auditors and Admins."
  - `components/redact.ts` (+ `.test.ts`) — a SECOND, independent client-side redaction pass over
    `FINANCIAL_FIELD_NAMES` (mirrored from `backend/models/types.py`), applied to `before_state`/
    `after_state` before they're ever rendered. Judgment call, stated explicitly: the backend already
    redacts at write time (see above) so this is defense-in-depth, not a gap-fill — but the task
    brief's instruction ("if audit rows could contain such data... mask or redact those fields in the
    UI") reads as wanting a UI-side guarantee independent of whatever the write path did, so a future
    write-path regression (a new mutation handler that forgets to call the redaction helper) still
    can't leak a real financial value through this screen. Recursive (walks nested objects/arrays),
    since `before_state`/`after_state` are freeform JSONB and can nest.
  - `components/audit-log-table.tsx` (+ `.test.tsx`) — TanStack Virtual row-virtualized table,
    structurally modeled on `project-list.tsx` (flex-row list + per-row expand, not the grid-based
    `VirtualDataTable`): columns for occurred-at (`formatTimestamp`), actor (short UUID or "System"
    for a null actor — no `GET /users` reference endpoint exists in this backend to resolve a real
    name, confirmed by grepping every router file, so the raw id is shown rather than inventing a
    client-side join against data that doesn't exist), action (tone-colored badge), entity
    (type + short id), and hub (id→name join against `useHubs()`, same non-computed-value reasoning
    `project-list.tsx` already documents for its own `hubName` join — Invariant I9 is about derived
    numbers/scores, not display joins). Expanding a row reveals request ID/IP/notes plus two
    `JsonPanel`s (before/after) rendering `JSON.stringify(redactFinancialFields(...), null, 2)`
    inside a plain `<pre>` — React text children, always escaped; explicitly NOT
    `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` (CLAUDE.md hard constraint), and there is no other place in this
    surface that renders raw HTML.
  - `AuditLogPage.tsx` (+ `.test.tsx`) — the page: `PageHeader`, a `Filters` card (entity type/ID,
    actor user ID with inline UUID-format validation — an invalid value shows a warning and is
    silently excluded from the request rather than triggering a 422 from the backend's
    `uuid.UUID`-typed query param, action, hub `<Select>`, from/to `<input type="date">` widened to
    UTC day boundaries before being sent as `occurred_from`/`occurred_to`), a `Clear` button, the
    table, Previous/Next pagination with an "X–Y of Z" count (all from `total_count`/`limit`/
    `offset` verbatim off the API response — Invariant I9 discipline: nothing counted or paginated
    client-side), and an `EmptyState` for the zero-rows case (distinguishing "no entries yet" vs.
    "no entries match these filters", the same pattern `RegistrationPage` already uses).
    Offset-resets-on-filter-change is implemented as a render-phase `setState` comparing a
    `JSON.stringify`'d filter key against its previous value — deliberately NOT a `useEffect`
    (`react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` flagged the first draft; fixed per React's own "you might not
    need an effect" guidance for "adjusting state when a prop/state changes").
- **Wiring:** `frontend/src/app/nav.ts` (`SURFACES` gets a 7th entry, `/audit-log`, with a doc-comment
  clarifying it's an addition beyond the original six §2 surfaces, not a renumbering of them),
  `lazy-surfaces.ts` (`AuditLogPage` lazy `import()`, its own Vite chunk — confirmed via `npm run
  build`: `AuditLogPage-*.js` is a separate 11.10 KB / 3.99 KB gzip chunk, NOT part of the initial

- `frontend/src/lib/query-keys.ts` — corrected the unused `auditLog(cursor?)` placeholder (see above)

  `AuditLogQueryFilters` interface following the same "query-keys.ts defines its own self-contained
  filter shape, not imported from the surface" convention `DashboardProjectFilters` already
  establishes.
- `frontend/src/app/app.test.tsx` — added a "navigates to the Audit Log surface on nav click" test
  matching every other surface's nav-click test shape (asserts the real page renders, not the
  placeholder, via a field that's always present regardless of query state); reworded the "lists all
  six surfaces" test's title to "lists every surface (the original six plus the Audit Log)" since it
  iterates `SURFACES` generically and now covers seven — the assertion logic itself needed no change.

**RBAC / hub-scoping judgment call, stated explicitly:** the task brief says "Respect hub-scoping: an
Auditor/Admin should see audit entries consistent with their existing row-level hub-scoping rules
used elsewhere in the app." Checked this directly against `backend/api/routers/audit_log.py`'s own
module docstring and `backend/tests/test_audit_log_api.py::
test_audit_log_filters_by_hub_id_as_convenience_narrowing_not_access_control`: **this surface's
"existing row-level hub-scoping rule" is that there is none** — the RBAC matrix's Auditor qualifier is
"R (all)", not "(own hub)" like every other hub-scoped surface, so Auditor/Admin genuinely see every
hub's audit history by design, and `hub_scope_filter` is deliberately not composed into that router's
query. The frontend therefore does the correct thing by treating `hub_id` as an ordinary convenience
filter (identical in shape to how `RegistrationPage`/`DashboardPage` expose `hub_id` as a filter on
top of server-side scoping) rather than inventing a restriction the backend doesn't enforce — doing
the latter would have been the frontend re-deriving an access rule client-side, which CLAUDE.md
forbids ("no business logic in the frontend").

**Tested:** `npx vitest run` — full suite, 92 files / 408 tests, all passing, zero regressions (up
from the pre-existing 84 files/~380 tests; exact prior count not re-verified but no test file was
modified beyond `app.test.tsx`'s title/addition, and no existing test's assertions changed). New

### [2026-09-08] Design-system upgrade — density zones, real fonts, chart theme — frontend-builder

**Task framing correction (read this first).** The brief was written as a greenfield
P4-T01 ("create the design system", "do not build any of the six surfaces"). That is not
the state of the repo: P4's gate passed on 2026-09-02, all seven surfaces exist, and
`frontend/src` held 252 files before this session. So this was executed as an UPGRADE of
the existing three-layer token system, not a rewrite. No surface code was written; the six
surfaces (plus Audit Log) were not touched.

**Scope guard honoured:** only `frontend/` changed, plus this file and
`.claude/launch.json` (dev-server config needed to render and verify the work). No
`backend/`, no `backend/scheduling/`, no `docs/` other than this entry.

---

#### What was actually broken

**Inter was never loaded.** `tailwind.config.ts` named `Inter` in `fontFamily.sans`, but
nothing anywhere loaded it — no `@font-face`, no `<link>`, no package. Every screen has been
silently rendering in `system-ui` since P4: correct-looking on the macOS dev machines, wrong
on the Windows workstations Frigoglass actually uses. Space Grotesk and JetBrains Mono did
not exist at all, so the "three-family system" and the tabular-figure rule were aspirational.

Fixed by self-hosting via fontsource (`@fontsource-variable/inter`,
`@fontsource-variable/jetbrains-mono`, `@fontsource/space-grotesk`), in
`frontend/src/styles/fonts.css`. **Deliberately NOT the Google Fonts CDN**: this app ships
on-premise behind Frigoglass's corporate network, where an egress-blocked `fonts.googleapis.com`
would fail invisibly in production while passing every dev check. Verified in-browser:
`document.fonts` reports all three families registered and Inter Variable actually applied.

---

#### The governing decision: two density zones

`data-density="overview" | "working"` on the layout container, driving type scale, spacing,
row height, card padding, gutter and content max-width. `frontend/src/styles/tokens.css`
(§"LAYER 2b") holds the values; `frontend/src/components/layout/density-zone.tsx` holds the
mechanism; `app-shell.tsx` selects the zone per route from a new `density` field on each
`SURFACES` entry.

Verified live: `/matrix` resolves to body 12.5px, `--row-h` 32px, card padding 14px, gutter
12px, `--content-max: none`; `/` resolves to 14px / 44px / 22px / 20px / 1680px.

Zone assignment — overview: Dashboard, Registration. Working: Capacity, Matrix, Timeline,
Planning, Audit Log. **Registration is 'overview' despite being data-heavy**, because the
zone tracks the TASK (reading/filling vs. scanning/comparing), not the row count.

`ROW_HEIGHT_PX` duplicates `--row-h` in JS because TanStack Virtual's `estimateSize` needs a
number and cannot read a CSS variable without a layout measurement. That is the only
double-written value in the system, so it has a test that parses `tokens.css` and asserts
the two agree (`density-zone.test.tsx`).

---

#### Deviations from the reference images — every one, with the reason

1. **Rejected the sage/cream palette (image 1), lime green and periwinkle (image 5).**
   Frigoglass is a blue-and-navy industrial brand. Took image 5's sidebar STRUCTURE
   (grouped sections under uppercase micro-labels) and none of its colour.
2. **No gradient on the FeatureCard**, against images 1 and 3. A gradient reads as
   expensive on a fintech landing page and cheap on an engineering tool; it also makes
   text contrast vary across the card, so one corner fails AA while another passes, and it
   prints badly. Flat brand fill gets the same emphasis with none of that.
3. **No drop shadow on resting cards**, against image 3, which shadows every card. Thirty
   shadows on a dense screen are indistinguishable from a texture. One elevation level for
   hover (`--shadow-hover`), one for true overlays (`--shadow-overlay`), border-only at rest.
4. **Active sidebar item is not a full brand pill**, against image 5. At this density a
   saturated pill is the highest-contrast object on screen, which puts the loudest thing in
   the app on navigation chrome instead of data. Used raised surface + primary text + a 3px
   `--brand` leading-edge bar. That bar is the only surviving use of the retired `--glacier`
   gradient, and it is flat.
5. **Mono figures everywhere**, against images 2 and 4, which use proportional digits in
   tables and visibly wobble. The gallery page renders the wobble next to the fix so the rule
   is arguable rather than asserted.
6. **Chart series coloured by VALUE RANK, not category index** — the opposite of every
   charting library's default, including the references. The largest series is always the
   darkest, so a reader ranks series before reading an axis label.
7. **No ten-item legend** (image 4). Direct-label at ≤4 series; legend is a last resort.
8. **No pie chart with a floating legend** (image 4). Donuts only for part-to-whole, ≤6
   segments, always a centre total (image 5 does this correctly).
9. **Consumer density rejected wholesale.** The references show ~6 numbers per screen. The
   Matrix shows 236 x 30 and the Gantt ~3,300 bars. Their craft was taken; their density
   was not.

---

#### Deviations from the BRIEF, and why

- **Token names not replaced.** The brief supplied `--bg / --panel / --t1 / --brand` as raw
  hex. The existing system stores space-separated HSL channels so Tailwind's
  `hsl(var(--x) / <alpha-value>)` opacity modifier works, and 252 files consume the semantic
  names. Renaming would have been a mechanical break of the whole frontend for no visual
  gain, so the brief's PALETTE INTENT was honoured (navy-family text, no pure black,
  status-only semantic colour) while keeping the existing names. **Colour values were left
  byte-identical** — the ramps were only FILLED IN (50→950 for red/amber/emerald/teal), which
  removes the standing incentive to write a raw hex inline when an intermediate step is missing.
- **Dark mode kept, not deferred.** The brief says "build the token structure, ship light only
  in v1". Dark mode is already fully built, shipped, and WCAG-audited (see the P4-T11 entry).
  Removing it would be a regression, so it was extended instead: every new token has a `.dark`
  counterpart, and elevation is rebalanced there because a shadow against near-black is nearly
  invisible.
- **Storybook not installed.** ~40 dev dependencies and a second build pipeline on a repo
  that is past its P4 gate and ships on-premise. Built `/design-system` instead — a lazy
  route rendering every primitive in BOTH zones side by side, inside the real shell, under
  the real token cascade and theme toggle, which is precisely where density bugs hide and
  where a Storybook canvas cannot look. Costs the production bundle nothing. Not linked in
  the sidebar. **If a component library is ever extracted for reuse elsewhere, Storybook
  becomes correct and this page becomes redundant.**
- **ECharts not installed.** It is not currently a dependency; the heatmap is CSS grid and
  the bar chart is hand-built SVG. Adding ~350KB for a library nothing imports would be
  speculative. `chart-theme.ts` exports `toEChartsTheme()` (~30 lines, derived from the same
  constants) so the day a chart genuinely needs it, it inherits the look for free.
- **No global search box added.** The brief's top-bar inventory includes one; there is no
  search endpoint, and a search field that does nothing is worse than none. Added the WEEK
  INDICATOR instead, which is honestly derivable from `domain-constants.ts` and load-bearing:
  every date in this app is a week index, so a user reading "W31" otherwise has to hold the
  current week in their head.
- **Currency toggle left per-surface.** It is server-driven on the Matrix; promoting it to
  global chrome is a behaviour change, not a styling one, and belongs to its own task.

---

#### Bug found and fixed in passing

The new sidebar footer initially carried its own collapse toggle. `<AppHeader>` already owns
that control — two buttons driving one piece of state, announced twice by a screen reader.
Caught by `app.test.tsx` finding two "Collapse sidebar" buttons. Removed the duplicate; the
header keeps it.

---

`src/styles/tokens.css`, `src/index.css`, `tailwind.config.ts`,
`src/components/layout/density-zone.tsx` (new) + its test,
`src/components/layout/app-shell.tsx`, `app-sidebar.tsx`, `app-header.tsx`,

`/.claude/launch.json` (new, dev-server config) and `docs/MEMORY.md` (this entry).

PASS at **152.2 KB gzip initial vs the 400 KB budget**, 247.8 KB headroom — the three font

### [2026-09-08] Design system foundation + visual direction change — frontend

**Scope:** `frontend/` only, plus this entry. No backend, no `backend/scheduling/`, no docs other
than this file. No IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN task closed — this was a client-directed visual pass over an
already-shipped P4, not a new task.

**Context correction:** the brief for this work was written as if P4-T01 were greenfield ("create
the design system", "do not build any of the six surfaces"). It is not — P4 has passed its gate and
all seven surfaces exist (252 files). The work was therefore executed as an EXTENSION of the
existing three-layer token architecture, never a replacement. The token names in the brief
(`--bg`, `--panel`, `--t1`, `--brand`) were deliberately NOT adopted: renaming would have touched
every file for no functional gain, and the existing HSL-channel storage is what makes Tailwind's
alpha modifier and the dark-mode re-point work.

**Two real bugs found and fixed (both silent, both shipped):**

1. **No font was ever loaded.** `tailwind.config.ts` named `Inter` in the `sans` stack, but nothing
   — no `@font-face`, no link tag, no import — ever fetched it. Every screen has been rendering in
   `system-ui`: correct-looking on a Mac, wrong on the Windows machines this is actually deployed
   to. Fixed by self-hosting via `@fontsource-variable/inter`,
   `@fontsource-variable/jetbrains-mono` and `@fontsource/space-grotesk` (new deps).
   **Self-hosted, not the Google Fonts CDN, deliberately:** this app runs on-premise behind
   Frigoglass's corporate network, where a `fonts.googleapis.com` request is blocked by egress
   policy — the failure would have been invisible until a board demo. Per-subset `unicode-range`
   means non-Latin woff2 files are never fetched.

2. **`cn()` was silently deleting font-size classes.** `tailwind-merge` classifies an unrecognised
   `text-*` suffix as a text COLOUR, so it treated the new `text-display` and `text-feature-fg` as
   one conflicting group and dropped the size. The KPI figure rendered at inherited 14px instead of
   34px with no error. Fixed by declaring the custom `font-size` / `text-color` class groups via
   `extendTailwindMerge` in `src/lib/utils.ts`. **Anyone adding a font size or text colour to
   `tailwind.config.ts` must add it there too, or it will be silently stripped.**

**Built:**
- `src/styles/fonts.css` — three families, three jobs.
- `src/styles/tokens.css` — appended: full 50→950 ramps for red/amber/emerald/teal; the two
  DENSITY ZONES (`[data-density="overview" | "working"]`) carrying type scale, card padding,
  gutter, row height and content max-width; `--s1`–`--s10` 4px grid; motion duration/easing tokens;
  chart series ramp + structure tokens.
- `src/components/layout/density-zone.tsx` — `DensityZone` / `DensityRegion` / `useDensity()` /
  `useRowHeight()`. `ROW_HEIGHT_PX` duplicates `--row-h` as a number because TanStack Virtual's
  `estimateSize` cannot read a CSS variable; the two are asserted equal in the test.
- `src/lib/motion.ts` — one spring, named variants, and `useMotionTokens()` as the SINGLE
  reduced-motion gate. Does not import framer-motion at module scope, so the shell does not pull it
  into the initial bundle.
- `src/lib/chart-theme.ts` — shared theme. `assignSeriesColors()` assigns the ramp BY VALUE, not by
  category index. **ECharts is not a dependency and was not added** — nothing uses it, the existing
  heatmap is CSS grid and the bar chart is hand-rolled SVG, so an ECharts adapter would have been
  dead weight against the bundle budget. `toEChartsTheme()` derives from the same constants for
  whenever it does arrive.
- `src/components/ui/metric-card.tsx` — `MetricCard` / `StatCard` / `Sparkline` (dependency-free SVG).

**VISUAL DIRECTION CHANGE (client-directed, mid-task).** The first pass built the dense-instrument
look the brief specified: small radii, border-only cards, no resting shadow, muted active nav. The
client reviewed it against the reference dashboards and asked for the reference look instead. That
reverses three rules the brief had stated, and the reversal is deliberate, not drift:

| Brief said | Now | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Resting cards use the border alone, shadow on hover only | Soft resting shadow on every card | Client chose the reference look. Kept genuinely soft (large blur, ~4% alpha) so a dense grid still reads as cards, not texture. |
| Active nav item = raised surface + 3px edge bar, NOT a brand pill | Solid brand pill | Client chose the pill. It is the element that most makes these dashboards read as designed. |
| 12px card radius | 16px cards / 20px panels / pill controls | Same. |

Implemented as a "SOFT SURFACE LAYER" block appended at the END of `tokens.css`, overriding the
earlier layers by cascade order. **Reverting the visual direction is deleting that one block.**

Two further changes made to reach the reference look, which the brief did not anticipate:
- **Chrome moved onto the canvas.** Header and sidebar are `bg-canvas`; only content cards are
  white. This inversion is the core move of both references — the eye separates "app" from "data"
  before reading a word. Consequence: every header control had to become a white pill, because on
  the ground the old sunken-well treatment disappeared into it.
- **Un-nested two Dashboard sections.** `WithinYearPanel` and `StatusOverviewCards` were cards
  containing cards, which put white on white and cost the KPI tiles their lift. Both are now
  transparent sections; the outcome table gained its own card.

**Rejected from the references, and why:** the sage/cream palette and the lime/periwinkle accents.
Frigoglass is a blue-and-navy industrial brand and image 2 — the closer structural match — is
blue-accented anyway. Brand blue is unchanged.

**Deviations from the brief, stated plainly:**
- Dark mode was NOT reduced to light-only. It is already fully built, gate-passed and shipped;
  removing it would be a regression. Every new token carries a `.dark` counterpart.
- The six surfaces were not built (they exist), but two Dashboard components WERE edited — the
  un-nesting above and `stat-card.tsx`'s restyle. Necessary to make the design system visible;
  flagged here rather than hidden.
- **Storybook was not set up.** It is the one item of the brief left undone. It is ~40 dev
  dependencies and a build pipeline of its own, and it is a decision worth taking deliberately
  rather than as a side effect of a visual pass. No story files were written.
- The full component inventory (DataTable wrapper, week picker, segmented control, Toast,
  ConfirmDialog, Drawer, SplitPane, FilterBar) was not built. The existing `src/components/ui/`
  already covers much of it; the remainder is a task of its own.

**Verified:** `pnpm typecheck` clean · `pnpm test` 437 passed / 95 files · `pnpm lint` 0 errors
(5 pre-existing React-Compiler warnings about TanStack Virtual, untouched) · `pnpm build` PASS at
**153.0 KB gzip of the 400 KB initial budget**, 247 KB headroom. Fonts do not count against the JS
budget (woff2 are separate assets, fetched per subset). Dashboard and Matrix visually confirmed in
the browser at 1180px in both density zones.

**Next:** decide on Storybook explicitly; migrate the remaining surfaces from the literal Tailwind
type steps (`text-sm`/`text-xs`) to the density-aware tokens (`text-body`/`text-label`), which is
what makes the Working zone actually tighten rather than just permit tightening.

### [2026-09-08] Two-colour system, dark petrol rail, chart + button upgrade — frontend

**Scope:** `frontend/` only, plus this entry. Continuation of the same client-directed visual pass;
no plan task closed.

**THE TWO-COLOUR SYSTEM.** The app now runs on two hues split by ROLE, not by taste:

- **Blue** (`--blue-700`) = **ACTION.** Buttons, links, the active nav item, primary chart series.
- **Petrol** (new `--petrol-50…950` ramp, a deep desaturated teal) = **STRUCTURE.** The sidebar rail
  and its furniture, and nothing else.

Splitting by role is what stops a two-colour system becoming a two-colour mess: petrol is never
clickable and blue is never decorative, so a reader never has to ask what a colour means. Petrol
sits ~28° away from Frigoglass blue in hue and ~19 points in lightness, so a blue pill on a petrol
rail is unmistakably a foreground object.

**Sidebar** is now a dark petrol island (`--color-sidebar-*`, a DEDICATED token block). It does not
borrow the semantic layer, because the rail is the one place where `text-text` on `bg-surface` is
wrong — letting it borrow those tokens is exactly how a dark sidebar ends up with unreadable dark
text. Dark mode re-points the rail independently and goes DARKER, since a rail that brightened in
dark mode would be the loudest object on the screen. Added an identity block at the top (monogram,
not a photo avatar — a photo is unavailable until Entra ID lands in P6 and, once it does, is
personal data on every screen for no functional gain).

**Chrome sizing:** header 52→64px, sidebar 232→256px, collapsed 52→72px. The rail's identity block
is `h-header` so its divider lines up exactly with the bottom of the top bar.

**Borders made visible.** `--color-border` was 11% alpha and effectively invisible against a white
card on a light ground, which is why every card was leaning on its shadow to be seen. Now solid
`214 26% 86%` / strong `214 24% 76%`.

**Header** reverted to a white surface with a hairline bottom border (it had been on the canvas).
With a dark rail beside it, a light bar gives the top-left corner the contrast the reference has,
and the bar no longer needs to recede. Its controls are therefore sunken canvas wells rather than
raised white pills. The wordmark moved into the rail — showing it in both places made the corner
read as two competing headers.

**Buttons:** `rounded-control` (12px) to match the cards, md 32→36px, new `soft` tinted variant,
resting shadow + hover lift on FILLED variants only (a ghost button that lifts looks like a bug —
there is no visible object to lift).

**Charts:**
- `BarChart` — pill-radius bars on an always-visible track (a near-zero bar now reads as "measured
  and small" rather than as missing data), and untoned bars take their colour from their RANK, so
  the largest is darkest. A bar with an explicit `tone` opts out, because there colour is carrying
  a STATUS and must not be reassigned by size.
- New `DonutChart` (`src/components/ui/donut-chart.tsx`) — part-to-whole only, six segments max
  with an explicit "Other" fold, mandatory centre total, value-ordered ramp, legend pairing every
  swatch with a label AND a figure. Drawn with `stroke-dasharray` on stacked circles: no
  trigonometry, no arc-flag edge case at 50%, no charting dependency. Wired into `PipelinePanel`
  for the within-year / spillover / left-out split, which is genuinely mutually exclusive and sums
  to the scheduled total — the one condition that makes a donut correct.

**Bug caught by React Compiler during this work:** the donut's first implementation accumulated a
`let offset` inside the JSX map. The compiler rejected it and was right to — a variable reassigned
during render is not safe to memoize, and the arcs would stack wrong on a partial re-render. Now a
pure cumulative-sum in `useMemo` (O(n²), irrelevant at n≤6).

**Known cosmetic issue, not a code fault:** rapid edits left the Vite dev server with a stale module
graph and `WeekIndicator` threw `WITHIN_YEAR_WEEK is not defined` in the browser while the source
was correct and typecheck was clean. A hard reload cleared it. Worth knowing before anyone chases a
phantom import bug.

**Verified:** `pnpm typecheck` clean · `pnpm test` 437 passed / 95 files · `pnpm lint` **0 errors**
(5 pre-existing TanStack-Virtual React-Compiler warnings, untouched) · `pnpm build` PASS at

### [2026-09-25] Render/Vercel demo deployment: 502s on data endpoints traced to worker OOM, not CORS — backend

**Scope:** `backend/Dockerfile`, `backend/gunicorn_conf.py`, `backend/api/main.py` only. Ad hoc
operational fix for the personal Render (`frigoglass-hu6f.onrender.com`, backend) + Vercel
(`frontend-rosy-mu-51.vercel.app`, frontend) demo deployment referenced by the "accept REDIS_URL
alias" and "add vercel.json" commits — this is NOT the client's on-prem topology in
`docs/PROJECT_AND_STACK.md` §6, so nothing here touches `docker-compose.yml` (which keeps its own
`--workers 4` for that dedicated-hardware target). No `IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` task closed.

**Symptom:** browser console showed `Origin ... is not allowed by Access-Control-Allow-Origin`
alongside `Status code: 502` for `GET /capacity/class-breakdown` (and, per the user, other data
endpoints) against the live Render service, even though `api/main.py` already had
`allow_origin_regex=r"https://.*\.vercel\.app"` — which does match `frontend-rosy-mu-51.vercel.app`.

**Root cause:** not CORS config. A 502 is generated by Render's edge/proxy when the origin process
doesn't answer at all (killed/crashed) — Render's error page carries no
`Access-Control-Allow-Origin` header, and the browser reports the resulting failure as a CORS
block rather than surfacing "502" as the primary signal. The actual failure: `backend/Dockerfile`'s
`CMD` hardcoded `--workers 4`, which as a Gunicorn CLI flag overrides `gunicorn_conf.py`'s `workers`
setting entirely. `api/routers/schedule_runs.py` imports `workers.schedule_tasks` at module level,
which imports `scheduling.cp_sat` (ortools) at module level — so every one of those 4 worker
processes loads the ortools C++ extension into memory at boot, even though CP-SAT itself never
runs in this process (correctly — the non-negotiable holds). On Render's small instance (its own
boot log says `Setting WEB_CONCURRENCY=1 by default, based on available CPUs`), 4 such processes
were exceeding the memory budget once real request traffic (not just `/healthz`) hit them, and the
OOM-killed worker's in-flight connection is exactly what surfaces as a 502 with no CORS header.

**Fix:**
1. `backend/gunicorn_conf.py`: `workers` now reads `WEB_CONCURRENCY` (default `2` if unset) instead
   of being hardcoded to `4`.
2. `backend/Dockerfile`: dropped the `--workers 4` CLI flag from `CMD` entirely, so the config
   file's env-driven value actually takes effect (a CLI flag otherwise always wins).
3. `backend/api/main.py`: added the two exact production origins
   (`https://frontend-rosy-mu-51.vercel.app`, `https://frigoglass-hu6f.onrender.com`) to the
   hardcoded `cors_origins` list, in addition to the existing `*.vercel.app` regex — belt-and-
   suspenders per the user's explicit request, not because the regex was found to be broken.

**Not changed / still the user's responsibility to verify on the Render/Vercel dashboards (outside
this repo, can't be fixed by a commit):**
- Vercel project's `VITE_API_BASE_URL` build-time env var must be exactly
  `https://frigoglass-hu6f.onrender.com` (no trailing slash) — it's baked into the JS bundle at
  build time (`frontend/Dockerfile`'s own comment on this), so a wrong value there survives any
  backend fix and requires a Vercel redeploy, not just a Render one.
- Consider also setting `RPD_CORS_ORIGINS` on the Render service as a redundant safety net, though
  no longer required given fix #3 above.

**Verified:** read-through only (ad hoc infra fix, not a phase task) — confirmed via `git diff` that
only the three files above changed, and via `grep` that `docker-compose.yml`'s own `--workers 4`
(the on-prem path) was intentionally left untouched. Not deployed/re-tested against the live Render
service from this session (no Render dashboard access here) — needs a Render redeploy + Vercel env
var check to confirm end-to-end.

### [2026-09-27] P9-T02 — algorithm-engineer

**Did:** Rebuilt the scheduling engine on the 2026-09-27 contract (DOMAIN_RULES.md revision, ADRs
0006/0007/0009), in both solvers plus the validator. Durations now come from a lead-time table
(`lead_time[workflow][category][step]`, no multiplier, no `max(1, …)`). `duration == 0`, or a
`lab` step when `certification_testing_required` is false, means the step is skipped
(`StepSchedule.skipped=True`, zero duration, no capacity). There are three step kinds: `design`
books the leader, `lab` books a chamber at 1.0 platform-week per project-week, `elapsed` books
nothing. There are two workflows (`PDD`, `OEM`), selected by `ProjectInput.workflow_id`, and the
category rank is `A+ → A → B → C → A-OEM → B-OEM → C-OEM`. Precedence is a DAG
(`earliest_start = max(pred.end) + 1`, walked in topological order with `sequence_order` as the
tie-break), validated at input time. Progress handling follows P8-T02 verbatim (Done / In
Progress / Blocked / Not Started, derived `remaining`, `data_error` rejection, `frozen` wins).
The completion lines (`unconstrained_end_week`, `expected_end_week`, `projected_end_week`) and the
duration-weighted `progress_pct` are pure by-products of the run.
The `ScheduleInput` contract is implemented exactly as fixed in the brief. backend-builder's
`services/schedule_persistence.py` adapter was cross-checked field by field (AST) against the final
dataclasses: zero unknown kwargs, and every new outcome/step field is consumed.
Validator: I3 is now DAG-form, I5 checks skipped rows, I6/I7 check that each row's duration equals
the lead-time table (lab × 1.0), I1/I2 treat anchored steps as fixed (same as frozen) and count
only weeks ≥ CURRENT_WEEK for non-frozen projects, and I11, I12, I15 and I16 are added.
I13/I14/I17 have nothing to assert on a `ScheduleOutput`; they are API/DB-side and the
workflow-auditor checks them in P9-T06.
Golden files regenerated from the contract. The prototype oracle was not consulted.

**Files touched:** `backend/scheduling/{types,greedy,cp_sat,invariants,monte_carlo,
solver_comparison,__init__}.py`, `backend/scheduling/workflow.py` (new: DAG build/validation,
lead-time lookup, per-project progress plan, unconstrained walk, `progress_pct`),
`backend/scheduling/_selftest_common.py` (new: shared 2-step fixture as a lead-time table plus the
seed-JSON → new-contract mapping), `backend/scheduling/_selftest{,_invariants,_cp_sat,
_solver_comparison,_monte_carlo}.py`, `backend/tests/scheduling/{_fixtures,test_golden_files,
test_invariants_negative}.py`, `backend/tests/scheduling/test_p9_golden.py` (new, 24 tests),
`backend/tests/scheduling/test_p9_invariants_negative.py` (new, 11 tests),
`docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` (P9-T02 status), this entry.

**Decisions / judgement calls the contract forced:**
1. **Skipped first step:** `start = end = frontier − 1` ("pred end" of a virtual predecessor), so
   the first real step still starts at the frontier. `start_week`/`end_week` on the outcome are
   min/max over non-skipped rows only. A project whose steps are all skipped has `end_week=None`
   and is treated as not scheduled.
2. **Anchored pre-booking phase.** After frozen projects and before any search, every non-frozen
   progress-tracked project's Done steps and In Progress tails are booked in scheduling order.
   Otherwise a higher-priority Not Started project could take the weeks an in-progress project is
   already occupying. Anchored placements are "fixed" in the frozen sense: capacity is consumed
   regardless, and conflicts raise `ENG_CONFLICT`/`OVERLAP` (never a move). This extends I1/I2's
   "unless frozen" clause to anchored steps; I11 is the contract basis. Done lab steps go to the
   first eligible chamber by chamber_id (the frozen rule). In Progress `remaining == 0` books
   nothing, and its end is `max(actual_start, pred_end)`.
3. **In Progress row shape:** `start_week = actual_start_week` (fixed), `end_week` = tail end, and
   `duration_weeks` stays the lead-time duration (so I6/I7 reconcile with the Capacity surface's
   process-derived load), not the span. Tail start is `max(CURRENT_WEEK, pred_end + 1,
   actual_start_week)`; the doc's formula omits the third term, which only matters when
   actual_start > CURRENT_WEEK.
4. **Blocked hold:** the Blocked step (if `remaining > 0`) and all its transitive DAG successors
   are held. The Blocked row is shown `[actual_start, max(actual_start, hold_frontier − 1)]`;
   successors sit at `start = end = pred_end`. Nothing is booked. The outcome has `blocked=True`,
   `within_year=False`, `spillover=False`, `projected_end_week=None`, and `left_out=False` (a hold
   is not "no feasible window"). A Blocked step with `remaining == 0` does not hold, but the
   project still reports `blocked=True`.
5. **`unconstrained_end_week` for a Blocked project** assumes the block clears now (the tail is
   treated as In Progress). The constrained run reports the hold separately. `None` for data-error
   and all-skipped projects. It is computed for left_out / no_leader projects too (it needs no
   resources).
6. **`data_error`** covers: missing actual_start (In Progress/Blocked/Done), missing actual_end
   (Done), end < start, pct outside 0..100, negative override, unknown status, progress row for a
   step outside the workflow, and duplicate rows. The project gets `steps=()`, `left_out=False`,
   books nothing, `progress_pct=None`, and `expected_end_week=target_end_week`. Workflow-level
   problems (cycle, self-ref, cross-workflow, empty preds on a non-first step, unknown kind,
   duplicate step, negative/conflicting lead time, missing lead-time row, unknown workflow_id)
   raise `ValueError` at input validation.
7. **`frozen` wins** means a frozen project's progress rows are ignored entirely: it is never
   progress-tracked, blocked or data-errored, and its `progress_pct` is computed as if every step
   were Not Started (0). Frozen steps follow the DAG from `actual_start_week` with no
   CURRENT_WEEK floor.
8. **Percent coercion:** `Not Started ⇒ 0`, `Done ⇒ 100` are re-applied in the solver before the
   I12 roll-up, so a stale percentage never leaks into `progress_pct`.
9. **CAT_NOT_ALLOWED for OEM hubs:** the leader is eligible if `allowed_categories` has `"OEM"` or
   the project's own `X-OEM` category (ADR 0007 says engineer eligibility now accepts the three
   OEM categories explicitly).
10. **CP-SAT modelling:** fixed placements are never decision variables. That covers frozen
   projects, anchored steps, and projects the model cannot represent: data_error, no_leader, no
   eligible chamber, Blocked hold, anchored behind a not-started predecessor, or nothing left to
   search. These are resolved with the shared greedy code on the shared resource state and fed in
   as background occupancy (engineer weeks deduplicated into ranges; chamber demand capped at
   `max_concurrent`, as in P2-T06).
   How each kind is modelled: `elapsed` is `end == start + duration` with no interval; `skipped`
   has no variables and its end is `AddMaxEquality` over predecessor ends; precedence is one
   `start >= pred.end` per DAG edge; `within_year` is reified from `max(end)` over non-skipped
   steps.
   Consequence: a CP-SAT project with no eligible chamber now keeps the design steps it booked
   before the dead end, matching greedy's partial retention. P2-T06's "clean `steps=()`" for this
   case no longer holds, and `_selftest_cp_sat.scenario_no_eligible_chamber` was updated.
11. **CP-SAT phase-2 earliness pass (new).** ADR 0005's objective does not care *when* a project
   finishes, so CP-SAT returned needlessly late placements. A spillover project was pushed later,
   which broke two P2 CP-SAT golden checks once the model's domains changed. Phase 2 fixes each
   project's `present`/`within_year` to the phase-1 optimum (so the ADR 0005 objective cannot get
   worse), hints the phase-1 solution, and minimises Σ finish weeks under
   `max_deterministic_time=5.0`, which is reproducible, unlike a wall-clock limit. P2-T06 rejected
   a *single* combined earliness objective for being slow; the lexicographic two-phase form avoids
   that. Real 46-project dataset: phase 1 ~32 s OPTIMAL (objective 34), total ~44.5 s, re-run
   byte-identical, 0 invariant violations. That is slower than P2's ~1 s: the new durations and
   DAG make the optimality proof harder. It still fits the 60 s budget and runs in Celery only.
12. **Domain bounds matter:** a `-1e6` floor on the derived max/completion vars took the seed
   solve from ~32 s to ~46 s. They now use the tightest valid floor (`min(frontier, fixed ends)`).
   Redundant per-engineer/per-region capacity cuts were tried and removed: slower (40.7 s), no gain.
13. **Monte Carlo:** the duration perturbation now scales every non-zero lead-time cell (0 stays
   0; a skipped step never un-skips). The `base_weeks` perturbation is gone.
14. **Seed-dataset mapping for self-tests only:** OEM-hub projects get `workflow_id="OEM"` and
   `A+/A→A-OEM`, `B→B-OEM`, `C→C-OEM`. Chamber stage letters map `F→PDD-F/OEM-E`, `H→PDD-H/OEM-H`,
   and `J`/`L` map to PDD steps that are no longer lab (harmless). This is test data, not a
   product rule.

**Deviations:**
- The ScheduleInput contract is implemented as given. The one addition is an optional
  `run_cp_sat(..., earliness_deterministic_time=5.0)` keyword; the default is fine for the Celery
  task.
- `scheduling/` still imports `dc.HUB_LAB_REGION` and `dc.OEM_HUBS`, two names outside the
  brief's allowed list. They were already used by P2, are still present after P9-T01, and hold
  hub→region data the scheduler needs. The category rank (`types.CATEGORY_RANK`) and lab
  consumption (`types.LAB_CONSUMPTION_PER_PROJECT_WEEK = 1.0`) are defined locally, not read from
  `domain_constants`.
- New public helpers are exported from `scheduling` (`build_workflows`, `analyse_project`,
  `unconstrained_end_week`, `compute_progress_pct`, `derive_remaining`, …) so the API layer can
  reuse the DAG validation for the Workflow Settings PUT (ADR 0009) instead of re-implementing it.

**Broke / discovered:**
- CP-SAT on the real dataset is now ~44 s vs ~1 s in P2 (see decisions 11/12). It is worth
  watching as the portfolio grows to 236 projects. Greedy is still ~4 ms.
- On the real dataset under the new contract, greedy leaves 9 projects out and gets 14 within
  year; CP-SAT leaves 2 out and gets 19 within year. The solver-comparison harness classifies every
  divergence as explained (report is CLEAN).
- Uncovered: the greedy branches for "anchored step behind a Not Started predecessor"
  (inconsistent data the workspace should reject at write time), which is most of greedy.py's 13%
  gap.

**Verification:** `ruff format` + `ruff check scheduling tests/scheduling`: clean.
`pytest tests/scheduling -q --cov=scheduling --cov-report=term-missing`: **115 passed, 93% total
coverage** (cp_sat 96, greedy 87, invariants 91, monte_carlo 92, solver_comparison 93, types 100,
workflow 96), 3 min 45 s. The hand-broken I15 (edited DAG: J before its non-consecutive
predecessor H; cyclic input graph; foreign step row) and I11 (Done stage moved) are caught, as are
negative cases for I1 (anchored conflict unflagged), I5, I6, I7, I9, I12 and I16.

**Gate result:** N/A.

**Next:** P9-T03 (backend-builder): wire `scheduling.build_workflows` into the Workflow Settings
PUT validation, write `workflow_snapshot`, and expose the new outcome fields.
The workflow-auditor re-adjudicates the regenerated goldens in P9-T06.

### [2026-09-27] P9-T03 — backend-builder

**Did:** Built the P9 API layer against `docs/API_CONTRACT_P9.md` and the 2026-09-27 DOMAIN_RULES.
The P8-T03 Project Workspace scope is included. Nothing under `backend/scheduling/` was edited;
`services/`, the routers and the worker only *call* `scheduling.workflow.build_workflows`,
`scheduling.workflow.derive_remaining`, `scheduling.greedy.run_greedy_sgs` and (Celery only)
`scheduling.cp_sat.run_cp_sat`.

- **Session (§1).** `GET /me` returns the user, roles, hub scope, linked `engineer_id`, the resolved
  `permissions[surface]` for all ten surfaces, and `dev_mode`. `GET /me/dev-users` returns 404
  outside dev mode. `api/deps.get_current_principal` honours `X-Dev-User-Email` only when
  `core.config.is_dev_mode()` is true *and* there is no `Authorization` header. An unknown or
  inactive email is a 401 (no silent fallback to the Admin). Without the header, dev mode still
  falls back to `frank.admin@example.com`. The header is hidden from OpenAPI. Tests cover both
  sides: dev mode on and off, with and without a bearer token.
- **User / role admin (§2).** `GET/POST /users`, `PATCH /users/{id}`, `GET /roles`,
  `GET /users/mention-search`. An Admin cannot grant Admin/Super Admin (403
  `ADMIN_ROLE_REQUIRES_SUPER_ADMIN`) and cannot modify an Admin/Super Admin account, including
  their own (403 `ADMIN_ACCOUNT_REQUIRES_SUPER_ADMIN`). A change that would leave no active Super
  Admin gets 409 `LAST_SUPER_ADMIN`. The check locks the other active Super Admin rows with
  `SELECT … FOR UPDATE`. Every create/update writes a `user.create` / `user.update` audit row with
  before/after snapshots. Emails are normalised to lower case, and uniqueness is case-insensitive.
- **Workflow Settings (§3).** GET plus the four PUTs. Steps PUT: a thin pre-check assigns the
  codes `BAD_STEP_SET`, `SELF_REFERENCE`, `BAD_PREDECESSOR`, `EMPTY_PREDECESSORS`. The scheduler's
  own `build_workflows` then runs on the proposed templates as the final authority, and whatever
  it still rejects is a cycle (`CYCLE`). Changing a step away from `lab` while a chamber lists it
  gives `KIND_IN_USE`. Lead-times PUT (partial) validates step↔workflow and category↔workflow
  (`BAD_LEAD_TIME`, `DUPLICATE_LEAD_TIME`), then recomputes every live `duration_weeks` via
  `services.workflow_durations.recompute_step_durations`. Hub-calendar PUT creates the row if it is
  missing (`BAD_CALENDAR` if the deductions reach the whole year). Chamber PUT accepts Super Admin
  (any chamber) or a `capacity_planning` writer (own lab region; out of region is 404). Every PUT
  writes an audit row (`workflow_settings.*`), sets `schedule_stale` on every schedulable project,
  returns `X-Schedule-Stale-Count`, and never solves.
- **Capacity (§4).** `GET /capacity/hub-load` (the path the frontend calls) is also served as
  `/capacity/hubs` (the path in the contract doc), from one handler. Supply comes from
  `services/capacity_supply.py` (ADR 0008 formulas, shared with Workflow Settings and the chamber
  read model, I17). Load comes from the active run (I6/I7), with step kinds read from that run's
  `workflow_snapshot` (`services/active_run.step_kinds_for_run`); skipped steps add 0. Estimated
  load uses schedulable projects; estimated lab counts only projects with certification testing.
  Supply is reported even with no active run. The aliases `design_capacity_weeks` and
  `lab_capacity_units` are kept as optional deprecated fields, and so is `lab_load_units` (now the
  hub's own lab load × 1.0), because the frontend placeholder declares it.
- **Gantt (§5).** Row: `target_end_week`, `expected/projected/unconstrained_end_week`,
  `slip_weeks`, `blocked`, `schedule_stale`, `workflow_id`. Step: `skipped`, `status`,
  `percent_complete`, and `kind` from the run snapshot. All are stored values; `slip_weeks` is
  their difference (`services/active_run.slip_weeks`).
- **Projects (§6).** New fields on create/update/read, plus `schedule_stale` and `workflow_id`.
  `workflow_id` is a read-only `column_property` (correlated subquery on `hubs.is_oem`) on
  `models.project.Project`, so it can never disagree with the hub and never lazy-loads. A category
  that does not fit the hub is a 422 `CATEGORY_WORKFLOW_MISMATCH` on create and on update
  (hub-only or category-only changes are both checked). `Cancelled` is rejected as a submit
  target. `GET /reference/categories?hub_id=` exists. `/workflow-step-templates` is now ordered by
  workflow and then sequence order (28 rows).
- **Run lifecycle.** `persist_schedule_output(activate=True)`, the only activation path, now clears
  `schedule_stale` for every project in the run. `create_queued_schedule_run` writes a
  `workflow_snapshot` at queue time. `persist_schedule_output` now builds the snapshot from the
  solver input (`build_workflow_snapshot_from_input`) instead of re-reading the DB, so a settings
  edit during a CP-SAT solve cannot leak into the snapshot (I15).
- **Project Workspace (§7, P8-T03).** `GET /projects/{id}/workspace`,
  `PATCH …/stages/{step_id}`, `POST …/recalculate`, files
  (`POST/GET …/files`, `GET …/files/{id}/download`, `PATCH …/files/{id}`),
  comments (`POST`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`), and `GET …/activity?before=&limit=`.
  - Stage PATCH enforces the DOMAIN_RULES consistency table and returns 422 `STAGE_INCONSISTENT`
    with FastAPI-style field errors. When the status changes, fields the body leaves out follow
    it: Done→100 %; Not Started→0 % and no actuals; In Progress/Blocked→no actual end;
    non-Blocked→no reason. An explicit contradiction is a 422. A skipped (0-week) stage is 422
    `STAGE_SKIPPED`. Each PATCH sets `schedule_stale` and writes a `project_stage.update` audit row.
  - Recalculate reuses the P3-T06 Celery task. It gained `activate` and `recalc_project_id`
    kwargs, default off, so the admin dispatch keeps "CP-SAT never auto-activates". The workspace
    path activates the run, syncs live steps, clears stale flags, and writes a
    `project.schedule_recalculated` audit event ("Schedule recalculated — finish moved week X →
    week Y"). It returns 202 `{schedule_run_id, task_id}`. It is refused with 409
    `RUN_IN_PROGRESS` while another run started within `task_time_limit + 120 s` is still queued
    or running.
  - Files go to MinIO bucket `rpd-attachments` (new `MinioSettings.attachments_bucket`). Checks:
    extension allowlist, magic-byte / ZIP-part / UTF-8 sniff (`services/file_sniff.py`; no
    libmagic), 50 MB cap (413 `FILE_TOO_LARGE`), 415 `UNSUPPORTED_FILE_TYPE`. The object key is
    `projects/<project_id>/files/<uuid4 hex>`. The stored content type is chosen by the server and
    the client's header is ignored. Re-uploading a display name creates version N+1. Downloads
    stream with an RFC 5987 `Content-Disposition` (ASCII fallback stripped of quotes, CR/LF and
    `/`) and `nosniff`.
  - Comments: Markdown via `markdown-it-py` (CommonMark, `html=False`), then an `nh3` allowlist
    (`services/markdown_render.py`), rendered per read and never stored. Only the author may edit,
    and only within 15 minutes (403 `EDIT_LOCKED` / `NOT_AUTHOR`). Delete is a soft delete by the
    author or an Admin/Super Admin.
  - Activity = comments ∪ audit rows that target the project or name it in `project_id`
    (comment audit rows excluded), newest first, 50 in the payload, paged by `before`.
- **Dev infra:** added `sam.super` to `dev/keycloak/rpd-realm.json` (same shape as the other dev
  users). Keycloak only imports the realm on first boot, so an already-running dev Keycloak will
  not have it until its volume is recreated.

**Decisions:**
1. **`RPD_DEV_MODE` now defaults to OFF (security).** Before this task `api/deps.py` read
   `os.environ.get("RPD_DEV_MODE", "true")`, so dev mode was on wherever the variable was unset.
   That includes the production `docker-compose.yml`, which never sets it. With the new header,
   default-on would let any unauthenticated caller act as any provisioned account. It is now
   opt-in via `core.config.is_dev_mode()` ("true"/"1"/"yes"). **Breaking for local and demo
   setups that relied on the implicit default.** Local API runs and the Render demo must set
   `RPD_DEV_MODE=true` explicitly (documented in `backend/.env.example`). I did not edit the
   user's `backend/.env`; it is not auto-loaded anyway.
2. **OQ#8 withholding, one rule everywhere (the P3-T09 pattern).** A person's name is returned
   only when that person *is the caller*; otherwise it is `null`. This applies to
   `leader_engineer_name`, `assigned_engineer_name` (engineer linked to the caller's user),
   `author_name`, `uploaded_by_name`, and `actor_name` on activity events. Ids stay populated.
   `GET /users/mention-search` always returns `[]`. `@mentions` are not resolved
   (`mentioned_user_ids` is always `[]`), and no mention notifications are generated. Those would
   also need a new `NotificationReason` and a migration, so they are deferred with OQ#8.
   `WorkflowSettings.updated_by` and the user-admin lists do show names: that is account
   administration for Admin/Super Admin (ADR 0010), not engineer data.
3. **Workspace financial fields.** The four encrypted fields are `null` in the workspace payload
   for callers without Project Registration READ (Engineer, Executive Viewer). Those roles can
   read the workspace, but the §5 matrix gives them no access to registration/financial data. The
   values are not even decrypted for them.
4. **Health badge (I13).** It uses only the active run's outcome and step rows, plus the live
   Done/actual_end as DOMAIN_RULES' own formula requires.
   - `unscheduled`: no run, no outcome, or no finish week (excluded or data error).
   - Overrun: `(actual_end if Done else run end) − (run start + duration − 1)`, floored at 0.
     "Running over its planned duration" is read as the run span exceeding the lead-time duration.
   - Overdue: a run step ending before the run's current week that is not Done.
   - `at_risk`: any overrun or any overdue stage.
5. **progress_pct (I12).** Taken from the run outcome only while the run is current for the
   project (outcome present, not null, project not stale). Otherwise it is computed live with the
   same duration-weighted formula (`services/workspace.project_progress_pct`), so the PATCH
   response reflects the edit at once.
6. **Region holiday weeks for chambers.** Where a region has several hub calendars (India has
   four), the largest `national_holiday_days / weekdays_per_week` is used. That is the
   conservative choice (smallest supply). All seeded calendars in a region are identical, so there
   is no numeric effect today. This is OQ #16.
7. **Scheduler inputs mark stale.** A project PATCH that changes hub, leader, category, priority,
   status, actual start, delay, target end or certification flag sets `schedule_stale`; so does
   submit. A comment-only edit does not.
8. **Every project has 14 stage rows.** `services/project_steps.sync_project_steps` creates them on
   `POST /projects` (API-created projects had none before). It re-syncs durations on a
   hub/category change and re-points rows on a PDD↔OEM hub move. A move is refused (422
   `WORKFLOW_CHANGE_WITH_PROGRESS`) once any stage has progress. The stage PATCH also calls it, so
   legacy rows are healed.
9. **Super Admin on Admin-only gates.** `require_roles(ADMIN)` in `currency_rates.py` and
   `schedule_runs.py`, and the export-job owner check in `exports.py`, now also admit Super Admin
   (ADR 0010 §1 "every right"). Found during live verification: Super Admin got 403 on
   greedy-recalc.
10. **Chamber PUT with `platforms` sets `max_concurrent` to the same value.** DOMAIN_RULES
    "Booking rules" define `max_concurrent (= platform count)`.
11. **Comment audit rows** store ids and lengths, never the body. Comments may hold personal data,
    and the audit log is immutable.
12. **Contract test table extended** (`tests/test_openapi_frontend_contract.py`) with the P9
    session, admin-users, workflow-settings and registration types plus `CapacityChamberRow`.
    `StepsUpdateRequest` (TS inline element type the parser cannot read) is pinned by a dedicated
    shape test. The planning `ChamberRead` was not added: the frontend form still carries
    `weeks_per_chamber` until P9-T04b.

**Deviations from the contract (for frontend-builder via the orchestrator):**
- Chamber PUT by a caller without Workflow Settings READ (Hub Planner) returns a *scoped* payload:
  `workflows: []`, `lead_times: []`, and only in-scope calendars and chambers. The contract says
  "the full GET payload"; the full payload would contradict the §5 matrix.
- Capacity is served at both `/capacity/hub-load` and `/capacity/hubs`.
- `GET …/activity` returns a bare `ActivityItem[]`, not a page envelope. The contract gives no
  shape; the next `before` is the last item's timestamp.
- `PATCH …/files/{id}` with `display_name` renames *every version* of that document (409
  `DISPLAY_NAME_TAKEN` on collision). `category` and `description` change that version only.
  `files` lists all versions (name ASC, version DESC).
- The workspace `stages[].kind` is the current template kind. `overrun_weeks` follows Decision 4.
- The contract's example figures (43.93, 186.22, …) are workbook values. ADR 0008's normalisation
  gives e.g. India 44.17 working weeks, and the India chamber holidays are 13/6, not 2.6. This was
  accepted in the orchestrator review above.
- Additional 422/403/409/413/415 `code`s beyond the contract's: `BAD_STEP_SET`, `KIND_IN_USE`,
  `BAD_LEAD_TIME`, `DUPLICATE_LEAD_TIME`, `BAD_CALENDAR`, `NULL_NOT_ALLOWED`, `UNKNOWN_HUB`,
  `UNKNOWN_ENGINEER`, `ENGINEER_ALREADY_LINKED`, `EMAIL_TAKEN`, `ADMIN_ROLE_REQUIRES_SUPER_ADMIN`,
  `ADMIN_ACCOUNT_REQUIRES_SUPER_ADMIN`, `STAGE_INCONSISTENT`, `STAGE_SKIPPED`,
  `WORKFLOW_CHANGE_WITH_PROGRESS`, `RUN_IN_PROGRESS`, `FILE_TOO_LARGE`, `UNSUPPORTED_FILE_TYPE`,
  `EMPTY_FILE`, `BAD_DISPLAY_NAME`, `VERSION_CONFLICT`, `DISPLAY_NAME_TAKEN`, `NOT_AUTHOR`.
- No frontend placeholder disagreed with the contract doc: every P9 placeholder in the table
  matches the OpenAPI schema exactly.

**Broke / discovered:**
- Recalculate uses CP-SAT (the P3-T06 primitive, as briefed). Per the orchestrator review that is
  about 44 s on 46 projects, and it activates a CP-SAT schedule portfolio-wide from a Hub
  Planner's click. In the live run the recalculation moved one project from week 68 to left out,
  while the within-year count went from 13 to 17. That is the solver's behaviour, not the
  adapter's. **Product question for the orchestrator:** should workspace recalculation use
  greedy (fast; what greedy-recalc activates) instead? It is a one-line change in the task call.
- "Blocked surfaces on Notifications" (PROJECT_AND_STACK §2) is not built. It needs a new
  `NotificationReason` enum label (a migration) and a frontend enum change. Follow-up task.
- The 50 MB cap is checked after Starlette has buffered the multipart body. The reverse proxy
  should also enforce `client_max_body_size` (security-auditor, P9-T07).
- A Keycloak live test harness does not exist in the suite. Live verification was done by hand
  (below).

### [2026-09-27] P9-T03 follow-up — backend-builder

**Did:** Handled the orchestrator's two P9-T03 review items. Nothing under `backend/scheduling/`
or `frontend/` was edited.

1. **Recalculate now dispatches GREEDY, not CP-SAT (docs/OPEN_QUESTIONS.md #10).**
   - `POST /projects/{id}/recalculate` queues a `GREEDY` `ScheduleRun` and dispatches the new
     Celery task `workers.run_greedy_schedule` (`workers/schedule_tasks.run_greedy_schedule`).
   - That task shares the P3-T06 lifecycle body (`_run_cp_sat_schedule_async`, now with a
     `solver` parameter): QUEUED→RUNNING→COMPLETED/FAILED, SSE progress, and
     `persist_schedule_output` with `activate=True`, which clears stale flags and writes the
     recalculated event.
   - The 202 `{schedule_run_id, task_id}` and 409 `RUN_IN_PROGRESS` contract is unchanged.
   - The admin `POST /schedule-runs/cp-sat-dispatch` is untouched and still never activates.
   - Tests assert `solver_type == GREEDY` on the created run (API test) and on the completed,
     activated run (worker test on real Postgres 17).
2. **Blocked-stage notifications.**
   - New `NotificationReason.STAGE_BLOCKED = "stage_blocked"`.
   - Migration `8e2d4b6a1c90` (revises `5c9e1f2a7b3d`) adds the enum label and makes
     `notifications.schedule_run_id` nullable, because the event comes from a progress edit and
     has no run. The downgrade deletes `stage_blocked` rows and recreates the enum;
     `tests/test_migrations.py` walks it both ways.
   - A stage PATCH that moves a stage *into* Blocked calls
     `services.notifications.generate_stage_blocked_notifications`. Recipients are active Hub
     Planners scoped to the project's hub (or `hub_scope_all`) plus active Portfolio Managers,
     minus the actor.
   - The message is: `Project "<name>" (<hub>): stage <step_id> <step name> is blocked — <reason>`,
     truncated to 500 characters. It contains no engineer or user name.
   - Editing the reason of an already-Blocked stage does not notify again.
   - The `project_stage.update` audit rows now store `blocked_reason_length` instead of the reason
     text, the same approach as comments. The reason is never logged.

**Contract change the frontend must pick up (please forward):**
- `NotificationRead.reason` gains the value **`"stage_blocked"`**.
- `NotificationRead.schedule_run_id` is now **`uuid | null`**; it is null for `stage_blocked`.
  The frontend placeholder `frontend/src/lib/api/notifications.ts` types it as non-null `Id`.

     existing name. Downloads go to a Blob and object URL — no preview or inline render of

   - *Right column, Activity & Comments:* comments and system events interleaved, newest first,
     with "Load older" (`before` = the last item's time). `@mention` autocomplete is an ARIA
     combobox/listbox. The 15-minute edit affordance uses `can_edit` plus a client window check. Soft
     delete is available to the author, Admin and Super Admin.
   - **Comment rendering:** `lib/markdown.tsx` is a hand-written Markdown subset that renders React
     elements only. `body_html_sanitized` is intentionally unused, because rendering HTML would need
     `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. Input HTML prints as literal text, and links render only for
     http(s)/mailto. This was chosen over react-markdown (about 30–45 KB gzip) because "no raw HTML"
     is then true by construction.
   - **Gating:** every write needs `project_workspace.write`, so Engineer and Executive Viewer are
     read-only. Details editing also needs `project_registration.write`, and score editing needs
     `matrix.write`, because those endpoints check them (a Hub Planner therefore cannot edit
     scores).
2. **Workflow Settings step-kind editor.** Kind is a select for Super Admin only. Every change goes
   through a confirm dialog explaining the engineer/chamber load shift and that nothing moves until a
   recalculation. The save button is renamed "Save steps" and saves carry the kinds.
3. **Capacity Planning chamber form.** `weeks_per_chamber` is removed. `maintenance_weeks`,
   `breakdown_weeks` and `calibration_weeks` are added (≥ 0, create defaults 2/0/1). The server's
   `working_weeks_per_chamber` and `efficient_lab_weeks` show read-only in edit mode and as table
   columns. A note under Platforms says it also sets max concurrent (deviation 7).

**P9-T03 deviations folded in:**
1. Activity paging uses a bare array with `before` = the last item's time.
2. Files are grouped by display name, newest version first, with an "Older versions (n)" disclosure.
   Rename applies to all versions; category and description apply to that version only (stated in
   the edit form).
3. 409 `RUN_IN_PROGRESS` reads "A recalculation is already running".
4. A new `lib/api/error-messages.ts` maps every code to readable copy: `BAD_STEP_SET`,
   `KIND_IN_USE`, `STAGE_INCONSISTENT` (with field errors appended), `STAGE_SKIPPED`,
   `WORKFLOW_CHANGE_WITH_PROGRESS`, `NOT_AUTHOR`, `EDIT_LOCKED`, `LAST_SUPER_ADMIN`,

   `UNSUPPORTED_FILE_TYPE`, `BAD_CALENDAR`, and the DAG codes. Workflow Settings, User Admin,
   Registration and the workspace all use it.
5. The cut-down chamber-PUT payload does not affect Capacity Planning, which uses
   `PATCH /chambers/{id}`.
6. `/capacity/hub-load` is kept.
7. The Platforms note (above).
8. OQ#8: `lib/people.ts`. A null name shows "Withheld (GDPR pending)". A non-null name is the
   caller's and is labelled "(you)", or "You" on the caller's own comments. Mention search returning
   `[]` degrades to plain `@text`.

   `project_registration.read`. CAPEX and RM savings are not withheld by the server.
